nodes.label: Wiki note C1.6A
nodes.note_text:
C1.6A | Drawing sheet — addendum-only (Add. 4 reissue) | Civil | Add. 4 (Feb 9, 2023) p.8; title block NOV 2, 2022; page 'XX of 96'; cites Addendum #3; revision block blank (Verified-Visual) | Addendum-only sheet with two plan views of existing-building areas showing process pipes to be routed below the existing concrete slabs where clouded in red (Add. 4 p.8, C1.6A — Verified-Visual). Pipes called out: 3-in 2W water reducing to 2-in before the sub-floor run to the dewatering skid, 2-in 2W water to the skid, 4-in pressate drain from the dewatering skid to the influent pump station, 2-in digested sludge (digester to pump; pump to dewatering skid), 2-in WAS (Train #3 to pump; pump to digester), 8-in secondary effluent from the Train #2 clarifier to UV disinfection, 4-in air from blower to digester, and 1-in 2W water from the bladder tanks to the 3-in 2W pipe (Add. 4 p.8, C1.6A — Verified). The sheet note requires concrete coring and/or saw cutting for access to sub-floor piping and cites Addendum #3 (Add. 4 p.8, C1.6A — Verified). Add. 4 p.3 governs the work: sludge piping runs below the existing floor in the clouded areas, all cuts are clean-edge by coring or saw cutting, floor repair matches the Blower Building slab design per Detail 8 on S4.1, and new rebar is doweled and epoxied with 4 in minimum embedment (Add. 4 p.3 — Verified). The base issue of C1.6A is not in the library (already flagged, 01 item 11). | Equipment: Under-slab process pipes (mapped to C1.3 IDs 7, 10, 15, 16, 19, 21, 23, 25 — Inferred); existing slab cut and repair; Spec sections: None cited on sheet; Sheets: S4.1 (Detail 8, via Add. 4 p.3); C1.3; Addenda: Add. 4 p.3 (C1.6A item); Add. 4 p.8 | C1.3; S4.1 and S2.3 (Structural & Building); C6.1–C6.3 (Process & Mechanical, not read)

33 05 00 | Spec section | Civil | Dec. 30, 2022 project manual (cover p.1); no addendum item | Supplements the drawings and WSDOT Standard Specifications for furnishing and installing all utility pipe and fittings, including trenching, over-excavation, bedding, backfill and trench dewatering; pipe must be new and sized as inside diameter unless it is a nominal-size product (¶1.01, ¶1.03; main spec p.413 — Verified; WSDOT Unresolved: external reference, not staged). Submittals: field-fabrication data, material certifications, and verification of every existing pipe to be connected (exposed and checked for size, material, elevation, location and service) (¶1.04; p.414 — Verified). Bolts and nuts are Type 316 stainless, thrust-block and tie concrete is 3,000 psi, and thrust restraint is not shown on the drawings and is incidental (¶2.01, ¶2.05, ¶3.018–3.020; pp.414–417 — Verified). Work near existing electrical and water services needs 3 business days' coordination with OPALCO, the Eastsound Water Users Association, the District and the Engineer (¶3.03; p.415 — Verified). Buried valves on ductile iron or nonmetallic lines get bituminous-coated nuts and bolts and an 8-mil polyethylene wrap; the section cites 'Section 01 30 00', which is not in the manual (¶3.025 B, ¶1.06 A.1; pp.414, 419 — Verified; see Issues). | Equipment: All buried utility piping and valves; Spec sections: 31 23 33; 33 31 00; 01 30 00 (cited; not in manual); Sheets: C1.3; C1.4; C7.2 (thrust blocking); Addenda: — | 33 30 00; 33 31 00; 33 32 00; 31 23 33; C1.3; C1.4

nodes.label: Wiki note 33 30 00
nodes.note_text: 33 30 00 | Spec section | Civil | Dec. 30, 2022 project manual (cover p.1); no addendum item; 02 decision D: cross-check Process & Mechanical for in-plant piping | General requirements for all piping systems shown on the plans, with trenching per 31 23 33 and submittals 'per Section 01 30 00' (not in the manual): field-fabrication data, shop laying drawings, pipe support drawings, material certifications and field welding procedures (¶1.01–1.02; main spec pp.420–421 — Verified; see Issues). Penetrations: poured-in-place DI wall pipe in slabs and walls, Link-Seal with 316 SS hardware (GPK sand collars for PVC) in new basins, core drilling in existing walls (grout at 6 in and under, Link-Seal at 8 in and over), and Link-Seal or Kor-N-Seal boots at precast manholes and vaults (¶2.01 C; pp.421–422 — Verified). All new piping gets #12 AWG steel-core tracer wire (Copperhead 1230-HS or equal) tied at 10-ft intervals, color-coded green for sewer, purple for non-potable and blue for potable, with Copperhead LD14/CD14/HS14 boxes whose locations are submitted before construction (¶3.03; pp.426–427 — Verified; conflicts with C7.1 and C7.4, see Issues). Testing is witnessed with 48-hour notice: force mains at 1.5 times operating pressure or 150 psi for 15 minutes (mixed liquor and West Plant Drain Pump Station force mains 150 psi, 2W and 3W piping 200 psi), HDPE per ASTM F2164, and valves with their pipelines (¶3.04.1–6, 8, 10; pp.427–429 — Verified). Gravity storm and sewer tests and water-line pressure tests and disinfection defer to WSDOT 4-04.3(1), 7-17.3(2) and 7-09.3(23), with DOH-lab chlorine (50 mg/L initial, 25 mg/L at 24 hours) and bacteriological reports (¶3.04.7, 9; p.428 — Verified; WSDOT test methods Unresolved: external reference, not staged).

33 31 00 | Spec section | Civil | Dec. 30, 2022 project manual (cover p.1); no addendum item | Material requirements for wastewater lines, with installation and testing per 33 30 00 (¶1.01, ¶3.02; main spec pp.430, 435 — Verified). Footing drains are 4-in perforated corrugated polyethylene per WSDOT 9-05.2(7); gravity sewer and drains are PVC ASTM D3034 SDR 35 or DI per WSDOT 9-05.13 (Class 50/51, cement-lined, poly-wrapped), with Sch. 40 PVC drain pipe at 4 in and under 'or as noted on the plans' (¶2.01 A, C; p.430 — Verified; WSDOT materials Unresolved: external reference, not staged). Pressure sewer is DI, PVC C900/C905 DR 18 or HDPE; buried 2W/3W water is PE4710 IPS HDPE DR11; buried WAS discharge piping is DI; buried aeration piping 4 in and larger is poly-wrapped DI, with stainless steel below 4 in (¶2.01 B, D, E, F; pp.430–431 — Verified; conflicts with C1.3, see Issues). Each 1-in yard hydrant gets two 3/4-in x 50-ft fire hoses and each 2-in yard hydrant two 1.5-in x 50-ft hoses; exposed DI is epoxy-coated per 'Section 09900' and above-grade wastewater pipe is insulated (Trymer 2000 XP) with aluminum jacketing (¶2.01 J–M, V; pp.432–434 — Verified). Water and sewer lines near each other follow Ecology's Criteria for Sewage Works Design C1-9, and floor drain piping points to 'Plumbing Spec 22 10 00', which is not in the manual (¶3.01 F, ¶2.01 C.3; pp.430, 435 — Verified; see Issues). | Equipment: Gravity sewer and drains; pressure sewer; aeration piping; 2W/3W water; WAS piping; footing drains; yard hydrant hoses; Spec sections: 33 30 00; 33 33 00; 22 10 00 and 09900 (cited; not in manual); Sheets: C1.3; C1.6A; Addenda: — | 33 30 00; 33 33 00; C1.3; C1.6A; 32 32 23

Fire hydrants are Iowa or M.H. 929T with a 5-in Storz port, shutoff valve 5–20 ft away, crash posts where exposed, a 200 psi hydrostatic test and a flow test, and installation per 'ESWD Standard Detail W-1', which is not in the library (¶2.011; pp.439–440 — Verified). The yard hydrant is a 1-in frostproof hydrant with a 1-in atmospheric vacuum breaker anchored to a post, and its callout points to 'Site Piping Plan, Sheet C2.2', which is the storm drainage sheet (Detail 1; plans_6 p.3, C7.1 — Verified-Visual; see Issues). nodes.label: Wiki note A1.1
nodes.note_text:
- **Document ID:** A1.1
- **Type:** Drawing — architectural floor plan with finish and door schedules, typical wall and roof sections
- **Discipline:** Architectural (Wilson Engineering title block)
- **Revision/Date:** Bid Set; title block NOV 2, 2022; seal 11-02-2022; revision "Ecology Review Comments" JGC 8/9/22 [plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual]. Reissued with red edits by Add. 4, issued Feb 9, 2023 [Add. 4 p.1, p.3, p.4 — Verified]; the reissue keeps the base title block (01 log #12). Add. 4 governs.
- **Summary:** The Blower Building is one room (Room 101, Blower Room, FF=23.30); Add. 4 resizes it from 42.00' × 9.50' to 44.00' × 9.25' [plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 4 and p.4 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. Add. 4 extends the new slab 9" north to abut the existing Train 2 building slab, has the Contractor field-measure and match the Train 2 finished floor, and states about 9" clearance between the buildings with the 10-ft setback kept from the south and east property lines [Add. 4 p.3, p.4 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. The base plan shows four blowers on a concrete blower pad 22.60' long and 4.50' deep (3" typical blower-to-pad edge) set 6.00' from the west wall (7.00' per Add. 4), an electrical panel bank with a 3.5-ft clearance note, two Ø24" bladder tanks per 1/C4.3, a 36"×84" motorized louver and a 24"×24" manual louver on the west wall, and two 24"×24" vents with exhaust fans on the east wall [plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 p.4 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. Add. 4 moves the MCC as far east as possible and adds a section (eight 20" sections, 160", spare section for future expansion), moves the MCP panel and its raceways, relocates the 2W bladder tank assembly per C6.4, and calls for 2 fire extinguisher assemblies (base shows 1) at wall locations coordinated with the Owner [Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 4, p.3, p.4 — Verified; plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 governs].

nodes.label: Wiki note A1.2
nodes.note_text:
- **Document ID:** A1.2
- **Type:** Drawing — exterior elevations and conceptual framing view
- **Discipline:** Architectural (Wilson Engineering)
- **Revision/Date:** Bid Set; title block NOV 2, 2022; seal 11-02-2022; revision block blank [plans_7 p.6 — Verified-Visual]. Reissued with red edits by Add. 4 (Feb 9, 2023) [Add. 4 p.3, p.5 — Verified]. Add. 4 governs.
- **Summary:** The four elevations show a single-slope (1:12) metal building with X-braced walls on a concrete foundation; Add. 4 changes the length from 42.00' to 44.00' and the width from 9.50' to 9.25' [plans_7 p.6 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 p.5 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. Add. 4 raises the building so both through-wall exhaust fans clear, taking the east-elevation minimum haunch height clearance from 9.00' to 10.25' and the floor-to-vent dimension from 6.75' to 8.00' [plans_7 p.6 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 p.5 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. The conceptual framing view (not to scale) has the Contractor provide a pre-engineered metal building with a similar column and bracing layout; Add. 4 sets a semi-flush girt at the high sidewall (5" from outside of column flange to outside of Zee girt flange), bypass Zee girts on all other sides, and Contractor means and methods for a weather-tight north wall with exterior metal panels that may be built on the ground and lifted into place [plans_7 p.6 — Verified-Visual; Add. 4 p.3 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. The south elevation shows door 101C at 5.00' × 8'-0", two door pairs of 5.00' leaves, and door 101B at 3.00' × 6'-8"; the west elevation shows the 7.00'-tall motorized louver and a 2.00' × 2.00' louver [plans_7 p.6 — Verified-Visual]. A footing-perimeter note calls for R-10 extruded polystyrene from top of concrete to bottom of footing, top chamfered 45°, exposed faces covered with grey Dryvit EIFS or equal, and metal-building-color flashing lapped at least 3" over the board [plans_7 p.6 — Verified-Visual].

nodes.label: Wiki note A1.3
nodes.note_text:
- **Document ID:** A1.3
- **Type:** Drawing — Blower Building interior elevations; existing office and WWTP building elevation details
- **Discipline:** Architectural (Wilson Engineering)
- **Revision/Date:** Bid Set; title block NOV 2, 2022; seal 11-02-2022; revision block blank; no Add. 4 entry [plans_7 p.7 — Verified (title block text); blocks Verified-Visual].
- **Summary:** Interior elevations of the proposed Blower Building show the four blowers, and the general note leaves process air and 2W piping off for clarity, pointing to civil sheets C1.1, C6.4 and C6.5 [plans_7 p.7 — Verified (labels); Verified-Visual (note, elevations)]. At the existing office building, the existing 4'-0" × 4'-0" louvered vent (south elevation) and 2' × 3' louvered vent (east elevation) are removed, the metal siding is replaced floor to eave with continuous siding to match (no horizontal seams), and the existing generator exhaust assembly is removed [plans_7 p.7 — Verified-Visual]. At the existing WWTP building, a new 3' × 7' louvered vent and a new 2' × 2' (24" × 24") exhaust fan are framed in, trimmed to match existing louvers and caulked, each marked "typical for all three locations," with final locations coordinated with the Owner [plans_7 p.7 — Verified-Visual]. Existing wall heights are shown as 9.50'± and the new exhaust fan is set 6.00' above the concrete slab floor [plans_7 p.7 — Verified-Visual].
- **Tags:** Equipment: blowers (4, shown); existing louvered vents 4'×4' and 2'×3' (removed); existing generator exhaust assembly (removed); new 3'×7' louvered vents (3); new 24"×24" exhaust fans (3) · Spec (by subject, Inferred): 07 92 00 (caulk); cross-lane 23 34 00 · Sheets: A1.1, A1.2; cross-lane C1.1 (unavailable), C6.4, C6.5 · Addenda: none
- **Related documents:** A1.1; A1.2; cross-lane 23 34 00 (Process & Mechanical, per 02 judgment call), C6.4, C6.5

- **Discipline:** Architectural

Running header reads 13 12 20 Metal Building Systems; body "SECTION 06 20 00 - FINISH CARPENTRY" governs — 02 conflict log #2, not re-raised [main spec pp.207–208 — Verified].

Execution covers coped and mitered trim, 45° splices, a sealed 1/8" gap at exterior trim ends, and installation of finish hardware and miscellaneous items on solid backing [¶3.1 A–I, p.208 — Verified]. No window, exterior trim or terminal board is shown on this lane's A sheets, so no ledger row maps to this section [A1.1–A1.3, plans_7 pp.5–7 — Verified-Visual; Inferred: the section may apply to items on other lanes' sheets].

nodes.label: Wiki note 07 20 00
nodes.note_text:
- **Document ID:** 07 20 00
- **Type:** Specification section — Division 07
- **Discipline:** Architectural
- **Revision/Date:** Main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (00 register: cover p.1, Engineer's Statement seal p.3); no revision marks on the section pages; no Add. 4 item [main spec pp.209–210 — Verified].
- **Summary:** Covers thermal insulation and vapor barrier in exterior roof and wall construction, installed by a metal building insulation installer with 3 years' experience; materials arrive with instructions and typical shop drawings, and the section has no separate submittal article [¶1.1 A, ¶1.2 A–B, p.209 — Verified]. The system is the Thermal Design Simple Saver interior finish and insulation system or equal — steel straps, woven reinforced polyethylene liner fabric with welded seams, sealants and tapes — with exposed parts at flame spread 25 or less and smoke developed 50 or less (ASTM E84) [¶1.2 C, ¶2.1 A–B, p.209 — Verified]. Insulation is unfaced fiberglass batt to the in-place R-value noted on the drawings (ASTM C518) with 1/8" × 3" XPS thermal blocks, and the vapor barrier goes on the interior side, continuous and taped at all joints and penetrations [¶2.2 A–B, p.209; ¶3.1 A–C, p.210 — Verified]; A1.1 sets R-25 walls and R-30 roof on furring with GWB walls, an assembly that differs from the liner system [plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual; Unresolved — Issues, Conflicts]. The section does not cover the R-10 XPS footing-perimeter insulation or the Dryvit EIFS shown on A1.2, and 02 lists no other Division 07 section except 07 92 00 [¶1.1 A, p.209; plans_7 p.6 — Verified-Visual; 02 index — Verified; Unresolved — Issues, Missing information].
- **Tags:** Items: Blower Building roof and wall insulation (R-30 / R-25), liner fabric, thermal blocks · Spec: 13 12 20 (by subject) · Sheets: A1.1 (Details 1–2), A1.2 (footing insulation — not covered) · Addenda: none
- **Related documents:** A1.1; A1.2; 13 12 20

nodes.label: Wiki note 07 92 00
nodes.note_text:
- **Document ID:** 07 92 00
- **Type:** Specification section — Division 07
- **Discipline:** Architectural
- **Revision/Date:** Main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (00 register: cover p.1, Engineer's Statement seal p.3); no revision marks on the section pages; no Add. 4 item. Running header reads 13 12 20 Metal Building Systems; body "SECTION 07 92 00 - JOINT SEALANTS" governs — 02 conflict log #3, not re-raised [main spec pp.211–213 — Verified].
- **Summary:** Submittals are manufacturer's data on materials, application equipment and procedures; the applicator needs 3 years' experience, and a 2-year special warranty applies [¶1.2 A, ¶1.3 A, ¶1.4 A, p.211 — Verified]. Exterior sealant is Dow Corning 795 silicone, clear, no substitutions (±12-1/2% movement); interior sealant is paintable acrylic-latex (Tremco, Pecora or Sonneborn) with Prosco R-Guard Air Dam at exterior wall conditions; sanitary sealant is silicone (±25%), plus acoustical sealer, closed-cell backing and primers [¶2.1 A–F, p.211 — Verified]. All concrete substrates are primed regardless of the manufacturer's requirements, and joints are half as deep as wide (1/4" to 1/2"), tooled concave, with sand broadcast to match adjacent concrete [¶3.1 A.4, ¶3.2 A, ¶3.2 C, p.212 — Verified]. 06 20 00 refers its joint sealant here, and A1.3's caulk at the new louver and fan trim maps here by subject; concrete joint sealant is a separate grey WSDOT 9-04.2 product under 03 30 00 [06 20 00 ¶2.1 D, p.207 — Verified; plans_7 p.7 — Verified-Visual; Inferred by subject; 03 30 00 ¶2.04 D, p.175 — Verified].
- **Tags:** Items: exterior silicone, interior acrylic, sanitary and acoustical sealants, joint backing · Spec: 06 20 00, 03 30 00 (concrete joint sealant, separate) · Sheets: A1.3 (caulk, by subject) · Addenda: none
- **Related documents:** 06 20 00; 03 30 00; A1.3; 02 conflict log #3

- **Discipline:** Architectural
- **Revision/Date:** Main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (00 register: cover p.1, Engineer's Statement seal p.3); no revision marks on the section pages; no Add. 4 item [main spec pp.214–215 — Verified].
- **Summary:** Exterior insulated hollow metal (INS HM) doors are standard-duty, full flush, SDI 100 Grade II Model 1 with polyurethane or polyisocyanurate core and 18-gauge minimum faces, of cold-rolled A366 steel hot-dip galvanized to A526 G90 with factory baked-on primer [¶2.01 A, ¶2.02 A, pp.214–215 — Verified]. Frames are one-piece welded, 16-gauge minimum, galvanized, with integral stops, SDI 100 Grade II Model 2, and tempered glass windows are provided only where the door schedule calls for them [¶2.02 B–C, p.215 — Verified]. Hardware is furnished under 08 70 00 and installed here per SDI 107, doors install per SDI 105 with hardware adjusted and lubricated, and the section has no submittal or testing article of its own [¶1.01 A, ¶2.01 B, ¶3.01, pp.214–215 — Verified]. The matching items are A1.1's insulated hollow metal doors 101A, 101B and 101C (Types A and B, no glass) [plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual].

nodes.label: Wiki note 08 70 00
nodes.note_text:
- **Document ID:** 08 70 00
- **Type:** Specification section — Division 08
- **Discipline:** Architectural
- **Revision/Date:** Main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (00 register: cover p.1, Engineer's Statement seal p.3); no revision marks on the section pages; no Add. 4 item [main spec pp.216–224 — Verified].
- **Summary:** Covers all finish hardware (quantities not guaranteed), with submittals of manufacturer's data, a hardware schedule in sets cross-referenced to the door schedule, a keying schedule and templates; closers carry a 5-year and other hardware a 1-year guarantee [¶1.01 A, ¶1.03 A–E, ¶1.05 A, pp.216–218 — Verified]. Part 4 sets Hardware Group 1 (exterior single INS HM doors) and Group 2 (exterior double doors): Stanley FBB179 hinges, Corbin Russwin ML2000 mortise locksets with Lustra lever trim keyed to the District standard, Ives 458 flush bolts and DP2 strike, Sargent 421 closers, kickplates, Pemko 357SP astragal, S88D gasketing and 315SN sweeps, National Guard 713 thresholds and Ives FS446 exterior stops [Part 4, pp.223–224 — Verified]; A1.1 assigns no group, so doors map by type [Inferred]. ¶2.03 A instead calls key-in-knob cylindrical locksets keyed to the "Upper Skagit Indian Tribe standard," and ¶2.07 A points the exterior door stop detail to sheet C8.1, which 01 does not list [¶2.03 A, p.219; ¶2.07 A, p.220 — Verified; 01 — Verified; Unresolved — Issues]. ¶2.08 A adds one concrete pad with a Gempler's #2900 boot and shoe brush with scraper next to the Blower Building exterior door, location coordinated with the Owner [p.220 — Verified]. Execution requires adjusting and checking every operating item, instructing the Owner's staff, a return visit about six months after acceptance to re-adjust all hardware with a written report, and 2 sets of special tools [¶3.04 A–E, ¶3.05, p.222 — Verified].

nodes.note_text:
- **Document ID:** 09 25 00
- **Type:** Specification section — Division 09
- **Discipline:** Architectural
- **Revision/Date:** Main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (00 register: cover p.1, Engineer's Statement seal p.3); no revision marks on the section pages; no Add. 4 item [main spec pp.225–228 — Verified].
- **Summary:** Covers all gypsum drywall shown, taped and spackled, to ASTM C840 from a single source, with texture finish samples as the only submittal [¶1.01 A, ¶1.02 A–B, ¶1.03 A, p.225 — Verified]. Board is 5/8" USG Aqua-Tough (green board) unless noted, Type X at fire-rated assemblies and Fiberock at high-moisture locations, with ASTM C1002 screws, Dur-A-Bead corners, LC and L beads, Perf-A-Tape and USG Imperial QT spray texture [¶2.01 A–E, p.226 — Verified]. Board fastens to steel framing with self-drilling screws at 12" o.c. max., gets a 3-coat joint finish sanded between coats, and hollow metal door frames are spot-grouted at the jamb anchors [¶3.02 H, ¶3.02 L.1, ¶3.03 D, pp.227–228 — Verified]. Texture primer is referred to "Section 09900 Painting"; Add. 4 adds 09 90 00 Service Condition J for the Blower Building's gypsum board, which matches the painted GWB walls in the A1.1 finish schedule [¶3.04 A, p.228 — Verified; Add. 4 p.2 — Verified; plans_7 p.5 — Verified-Visual].

nodes.label: Wiki note 09 90 00
nodes.note_text:
- **Document ID:** 09 90 00
- **Type:** Specification section — Division 09
- **Discipline:** Architectural
- **Revision/Date:** Main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (00 register: cover p.1, Engineer's Statement seal p.3); no revision marks on the section pages. Add. 4 p.2 revises ¶2.01 I to add Service Condition J — Add. 4 governs [main spec pp.229–235; Add. 4 p.2 — Verified].
- **Summary:** Covers preparation and application of paint coatings, but ¶1.01 A sends the new Blower Building and masonry, concrete and stucco painting to a "09 90 00 – Paints and Coatings" section that exists in neither the main spec nor 02 [¶1.01 A, p.229 — Verified; Unresolved — Issues, Missing information]. Submittals are product data and procedures per service condition, color charts 30 days and a painting schedule 14 days before work; the Contractor measures wet-film thickness of every coat, the Engineer approves each coat, and hold points follow surface preparation and final coating [¶1.03 A–C, ¶1.02 E, p.229; ¶3.03 D, p.234; ¶3.06, p.235 — Verified]. Service conditions are A epoxy (Tnemec 161 or SW Macropoxy 646) on exposed metal piping, valves, supports and misc. ferrous metal but not galvanized, aluminum or stainless; B interior wood; C metal doors and frames (two coats SW Industrial Enamel, DF 4.0, over factory primer); D PVC piping; E exterior wood stain; and H non-skid epoxy at the headworks floor [¶2.01 I.1–6, pp.231–232 — Verified]. Add. 4 adds Service Condition J for the new Blower Building gypsum board: one coat Sherwin-Williams wall primer (DF 2.0) and two coats Sherwin-Williams Pro-Mar alkyd egg-shell (DF 4.0) [Add. 4 p.2, 09 90 00 ¶2.01 I — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. Execution requires concrete cured 28 days before painting, galvanized surfaces passivated before priming, and exposed piping painted and labeled by service (for example, 2W light blue, air white) with a labeling walk-through before Substantial Completion [¶3.02 G and L, pp.233–234; ¶3.05, p.235 — Verified].

nodes.label: Wiki note 10 52 00
nodes.note_text:
- **Document ID:** 10 52 00
- **Type:** Specification section — Division 10
- **Discipline:** Architectural
- **Revision/Date:** Main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (00 register: cover p.1, Engineer's Statement seal p.3); no revision marks on the section pages; no Add. 4 change to the section; Add. 4 p.4 (A1.1) sets the Blower Building quantity at 2 [main spec p.242; Add. 4 p.4 — Verified].
- **Summary:** Covers furnishing and installing all fire extinguishers and cabinets shown, with product data (plus cabinet roughing-in and mounting details) as the submittal [¶1.01 A–B, ¶1.02 A, p.242 — Verified]. Extinguishers are J.L. Industries Cosmic 5E, UL 2A-10BC, standard red, on the manufacturer's standard brackets that prevent accidental dislodgment [¶2.01 A–B, p.242 — Verified]. At completion the work is visually inspected and checked for proper operation, and each extinguisher carries an inspection tag [¶3.01 C, p.242 — Verified]. Document ID: 23 34 00 | Type: Specification section, 3 pages | Discipline: Process-Mechanical (lane per 02, decision D; cross-check E9.3 and A sheets) | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); no section-level date
Summary: Scope (¶1.01 A p.265): in the Blower Building, two 3,300 CFM wall fans on individual thermostats, one motorized 36"×84" louvered vent that opens when either fan runs and stays open until both are off, and one manual 24"×24" louvered vent; in the "Existing Dewatering/Train 1&2 Building Area", three 3,300 CFM wall fans on individual manual on/off switches and two manual 36"×84" louvered vents. Fans are Acme FQ18G6 (3,300 CFM, 1/2 HP, 120 V 1-phase, 12 sones max) with wall collar and guard, each with a Louvers & Dampers EBE445 aluminum gravity combination louver (about 24"×24") with stainless bird screen and a 2-year minimum manufacturer warranty; thermostats are Schaffer TH109 two-speed, 40–100°F, in NEMA 4X enclosures with stainless coil sensors, 4' above floor (¶1.01 B; ¶2.1 A–B pp.265–266). Vents are "Pottoroff" (as printed) EXD-645 combination louver/dampers with drainable blades, vinyl seals, washable 18×16 stainless insect screens and non-protruding actuation; the motorized unit uses a Pottoroff AF120 120 V spring-return actuator driven from the fan thermostat auxiliary contacts (¶2.2–2.3 pp.266–267). ¶2.1 A.4 calls all wall fans dual speed and thermostat controlled, while ¶1.01 A puts the three existing-building fans on manual switches (Issue 25). The section has no submittal or testing paragraph; installation follows the manufacturer's instructions, with controls 4' above floor (¶3.1 p.267).

- **Document ID:** S1.1
- **Type:** Drawing — structural general notes: design criteria, foundations, concrete, anchorage, steel, submittals, special inspections
- **Discipline:** Structural (Kingworks Structural Engineers, KW job 21131, for Wilson 2020-070)
- **Revision/Date:** Title block 10-15-2021; revision 2 "Bid Set" TH 9/6/22 [plans_7 p.8 — Verified-Visual]. No Add. 4 entry. Page total reads "OF 98" — logged in 01 (#10), not re-raised.
- **Summary:** Design basis is the 2018 IBC, Risk Category III, 100 psf floor live load, 25 psf ground and flat-roof snow (Ct 1.1, Ce 1.1, Is 1.1), 105 mph ultimate wind (Exposure C), and seismic Site Class D (default), SDC D, Ie 1.25, SDS 0.79g, SD1 0.51g [plans_7 p.8, S1.1 General Notes 1–6 — Verified-Visual]. Foundations use 2,500 psf allowable bearing (×1.33 for wind or seismic), a minimum 1'-6" frost cover, and the GeoEngineers report dated September 7, 2021 (clouded, revision 2) for subgrade, backfill and compaction [plans_7 p.8, Foundations & Subgrade 1, 2, 8 — Verified-Visual; report-date conflict already flagged in 02 Unresolved spec items #2 and the 03 Merge flag — cited, not re-raised]. The concrete material schedule sets 4,500 psi and 0.45 max w/cm for three groups: Blower Building slab-on-grade, grade beams and misc. equipment pads (3/4" aggregate, 6% air, 30% min fly ash/slag); hydraulic structures (1" aggregate, air per notes, 20%); and the "Drain Pump Station Lid" (3/4", 5%, 20%) [plans_7 p.8, Reinforced Concrete 2 — Verified-Visual]. Minimum structural shop drawings are concrete reinforcing (including wall elevations), mix designs, a slab-on-grade jointing plan and structural steel; deferred submittals, sealed by a Washington PE, are metal stairs & landings and the pre-engineered metal building for the Blower Building [plans_7 p.8, Submittals 4–5 — Verified-Visual].

- **Summary:** The foundation plan shows two cast-in-place basins on 12" mat slab foundations — a UV basin with 8" concrete walls and a digester with 12" concrete walls — with an HDG W8×18 beam spanning the digester, connected to the wall at each end per Detail 7 [plans_8 p.2, S2.2 Detail 1 — Verified-Visual]. Mat slab reinforcing is called out twice as "typical for mat slabs this plan," once as #6 @ 10" o.c. T&B and once as #6 @ 12" o.c. T&B, and reinforcing at penetrations follows 6/S4.1 and 7/S4.1 [plans_8 p.2, Detail 1 — Verified-Visual; spacing — Unresolved: need engineer clarification, Issues, Conflicts #1]. Sections A-A, B-B and C-C show #5 and #6 wall bars at 10"–12" o.c. (each face in the 12" walls, centered in the 8" walls) hooked 3" clear from bottom, a hydrophilic waterstop at all construction joints (submit for approval), an unreinforced sloped concrete topping per civil, subgrade preparation per the structural notes and geotech report, and "guardrail & ladders per civil" [plans_8 p.2, Details 2–4 — Verified-Visual]. - **Summary:** Covers labor, materials and equipment for subgrade preparation, forms, rebar and placement of all cast-in-place concrete shown, paid as incidental to the lump-sum bid items in which the work appears; the only extra-work items are overexcavation and structural fill under 31 20 00, by written authorization [¶1.01 A.1, ¶1.03, p.172 — Verified]. The Owner provides independent testing and inspection (subgrade compaction and moisture, reinforcing placement, concrete placement and cylinders) and special inspections, and anchor bolts are set to AISC 303-16 §7.5 tolerances by a registered land surveyor [¶1.07 B, p.174; ¶3.012 A, p.180; ¶3.03 B, p.176 — Verified].

- **Document ID:** 05 50 00
- **Type:** Specification section — Division 05
- **Discipline:** Structural
- **Revision/Date:** Main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (00 register: cover p.1, Engineer's Statement seal p.3); no revision marks on the section pages; no Add. 4 item [main spec pp.186–199 — Verified].
- **Summary:** Covers metal fabrications that are not structural steel or other specified metal systems — embedded and non-embedded metal work, anchor bolts, beams, bracing, framing and supports for mechanical and electrical equipment, shelf angles, metal ladders and ship ladders, and metal pipe and tube railings — related to 03 30 00, 13 12 20 and 09 90 00 [¶1.01 A–B, ¶1.02, p.186 — Verified]. Submittals are shop drawings for all fabricated items, product data, nosing samples, PE qualification data, stainless mill certificates, paint compatibility certificates and welder certificates, with welding to AWS D1.1/D1.6 by state-licensed welders [¶1.04, p.187; ¶1.05 B, p.187; ¶2.04 A, p.192 — Verified]. Ferrous metal not fully embedded in concrete is hot-dip galvanized after fabrication (2 oz/sf min.), aluminum touching concrete gets bituminous paint, and all-thread hanger rod is allowed only in stainless [¶2.02 D, p.191; ¶2.010, p.193; ¶3.04 A, p.197; ¶2.08, p.193 — Verified]. Mechanical anchors are limited to non-water-bearing concrete (building slabs, walkways, Engineer-approved locations), and chemical anchors are required on all water-bearing structures and wherever spacing or edge distance is under 3.5" [¶2.03 B, pp.191–192 — Verified]. Handrails and guardrails are specified here as 1-1/4" steel pipe (ASTM A53 Gr B) while ¶2.02 B specifies aluminum pipe railings, and grouting is referred to a Section 04 60 00 that exists neither in the main spec nor in 02 [¶2.014 A, p.196; ¶2.02 B.1, p.191; ¶3.03 E, p.197 — Verified; Unresolved — Issues].

- **Document ID:** 05 52 00
- **Type:** Specification section — Division 05
- **Discipline:** Structural
- **Revision/Date:** Main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (00 register: cover p.1, Engineer's Statement seal p.3); no revision marks on the section pages; no Add. 4 item [main spec pp.203–204 — Verified].
- **Summary:** Aluminum handrails (two horizontal bars) and guardrails (6" sphere rule) are provided where shown, with height, picket spacing and toe plates detailed on the Civil Drawings, to OSHA and IBC 2018 [¶1.01 A–B, p.203 — Verified]. Submittals are shop drawings with a dimensional layout, the manufacturer's assembly and installation instructions, and calculations sealed by a Washington State registered structural engineer; partial or unsealed submittals are rejected [¶1.02 A–B, p.203 — Verified]. Rails, posts and stanchions are 1-1/2" IPS Schedule 40 aluminum with a clear satin anodized Class I finish (0.7 mil min.) from Golden Railing, CRL or Ametco or equal, with 3/16" min. aluminum toeboards on all guardrails [Part 2 A–B, p.203 — Verified]. Connections to structure use Type 316 stainless bolts, posts and rails get weep holes, removable sections mount independently, aluminum touching concrete gets bituminous paint, and embedded posts are grouted into blockouts after the concrete reaches design strength [¶3.01 B–D, ¶3.02 A–B, p.204 — Verified].
- **Tags:** Items: handrails and guardrails (locations per civil drawings) · Spec: 05 50 00 (conflicting steel railing, ¶2.014 A), 05 51 10 · Sheets: guardrail "per civil" on S2.1, S2.2 · Addenda: none

nodes.label: Wiki note 05 53 00
nodes.note_text:
- **Document ID:** 05 53 00
- **Type:** Specification section — Division 05
- **Discipline:** Structural
- **Revision/Date:** Main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (00 register: cover p.1, Engineer's Statement seal p.3); no revision marks on the section pages; no Add. 4 item [main spec pp.205–206 — Verified].
- **Summary:** Scope is aluminum grating set in pultruded vinyl ester FRP embedment angles with an integral anchor, to the NAAMM Metal Bar Grating Manual, with shop drawings and manufacturer's instructions as the submittal (the paragraph asks for a "dimensional layout of all handrailing," as written) [¶1.01 A, ¶1.02 A, ¶1.03 A, p.205 — Verified]. Solid plank grating is for UV channels only: 2" all-aluminum slip-resistant plank (SlipNOT or equal) that blocks all light from leaving the UV channel, on embedment angles per the grating manufacturer [¶2.01 A–C, p.205 — Verified]. Aluminum bar grating carries 100 psf at L/360 (2.0" deep, 4.0 lb/sf for 2'-6" to 6'-7" spans), is banded I-bar, and sits flush on 2"×2"×1/4" gray pultruded FRP embedment angles (IKG or equal) [¶2.02 A–C, p.205 — Verified]. Grating is fastened with removable aluminum clips and Type 316 stainless bolts, with galvanic isolation and bituminous paint where aluminum meets concrete or grout [¶3.01 A–C, p.206 — Verified]; S2.2 instead supports the grating on HDG steel angles and calls solid plank grating as typical at both basins [plans_8 p.2, Details 5–6 — Verified-Visual; Unresolved — Issues, Conflicts].
- **Tags:** Items: solid plank grating (UV channels), aluminum bar grating, FRP embedment angles · Spec: 05 50 00, 05 51 10 · Sheets: S2.2 (Details 2, 3, 5, 6) · Addenda: none
- **Related documents:** S2.2; 05 50 00; 05 51 10; 46 66 00 (UV channel, Process & Mechanical)

- **Type:** Specification section — Division 13
- **Discipline:** Structural
- **Revision/Date:** Main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (00 register: cover p.1, Engineer's Statement seal p.3); no revision marks on the section pages. Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 3 cites ¶2.03 and ¶2.04 (factory exterior and interior finish confirmed, no text change); Add. 4 building dimensions govern over ¶2.05 A.1 [main spec pp.246–251; Add. 4 p.1 — Verified].
- **Summary:** Covers a rigid-frame, bolted, pre-manufactured metal building with galvanized cold-formed secondary members and pre-coated metal roofing and siding, for the Blower Building and the existing building modifications shown on A1.3 [¶1.01 A–B, p.246 — Verified]. Design loads — 5 psf collateral, 25 psf snow, 20 psf roof live, 105 mph ultimate wind (Exposure C), Site Class D with SDS 0.79 / SD1 0.51, SDC D, Ie 1.25, 18" frost — match S1.1, and submittals are WA SE-sealed design calculations and drawings for permit, a WA SE-sealed anchor bolt embedment design by the Contractor, and erection drawings [¶1.03 A, p.246; ¶1.04 A–B, p.247 — Verified; plans_7 p.8 — Verified-Visual]. Garco Building Systems or equal (AISC Category MB certified, MBMA member) supplies 50 ksi hot-dip galvanized primary framing, G-90 16-gauge secondary members, A325 bolts, galvanized cable or rod bracing, 24-gauge Galvalume standing-seam roof panels (UL 90) and 26-gauge Galvalume R- or A-type wall panels, factory-finished in polyester or Kynar at the Owner's choice [¶1.05, ¶2.01–¶2.04, pp.247–249 — Verified; Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 3 — Verified]. ¶2.05 A.1 describes the Blower Building as a rigid frame of "42' bldg. width, 9.75' bldg. length" with 9'-0" minimum haunch clearance, which Add. 4 supersedes with a 44.00' × 9.25' footprint and 10.25' clearance [p.249 — Verified; Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 4, p.4, p.5 — Verified; Add. 4 governs].

Document ID: C5.1 | Type: Drawing — plan view and grating & guardrail plan | Discipline: Civil (per 01); process-mechanical content | Revision/Date: BID SET; title block NOV 2, 2022; seal 11-02-2022; revisions "Add UV Disinfection" JGC 5/10/22 and "Ecology Review Comments" JGC 8/9/22
Summary: One concrete structure about 45.00' × 13.00' (44.00' and 12.00' inside dimensions shown) holds the UV disinfection chamber (UV Channels #1 and #2), an effluent sample chamber ("effluent sample location") and the aerobic digester; section cuts A–D refer to C5.2 and C5.3. An 8" inlet splits to the two channels through 8" gate valves with hand wheels (keyed note 5); each channel holds a bank of UV modules with 1" drains, work areas sloped 1% minimum, rim EL 18.74 and TOC 18.83, with two wall-mounted control panels, aluminum access ladders (nominal 2' wide, keyed note 4) and a 4" UV drain with 4" gate valves (keyed note 3). The digester (TOC 15.3 down to 14.3; floor slopes 2.4%, 3.1% and 8.3%; 6" lip all around) has 3" and 4" air lines, an HDG I-beam ("see structural"), a 4" T-valve on a 4" supernatant drain pipe, a 2" SCH 80 PVC digested sludge outlet, a 3" WAS line, a 4" drain and wall-mount pipe supports per 7/C7.2 (keyed note 6); link-seal boots seal all pipe-to-concrete connections (keyed note 1). The grating & guardrail plan shows guardrail with removable guard chains (4 locations) around the UV chamber, a removable guard chain with a 2'-8" opening at the effluent sample chamber, and removable grating over the aerobic digester. 01 sets this sheet to Text, but its text layer holds only UV module labels (LAMP/STATUS/TOP/BOTTOM) and view titles, so the plan content above was read from the image.

Summary: Section A cuts the UV chamber (top of wall 23.80, FG 23.3 sloping 2% away, bottom elev 17.74, TOC 18.83 and 19.08) and the aerobic digester (top of wall 26.80, bottom EL 13.3, with a 1-ft thick lip projecting 1/2 ft all around for anti-buoyancy). On the UV side the 8" influent pipe (IE 19.61) enters past a valve hand wheel, the unit runs from HWL 21.49 to HWL 21.09 over a weir level control, with 1" drains, a 2"×1" reducer and 1" PVC ball valve, a floor drain (rim 18.74, IE 16.00), a wall control panel, and the 10" effluent pipe leaving at IE 18.75 (IE 19.44 also shown); guardrail tops are 42" above finish grade (field adjust) and a prefab aluminum ladder connects to the access platform. Between the chambers the labels TOC 17.25, bottom elev 16.25 and a 4" drain pipe at IE 17.25 fall in the effluent sample chamber (location Inferred from C5.1). On the digester side, 3" SS air pipes (centerlines 27.3 and 25.8) on 4 wall-mount pipe supports per 7/C7.2 feed 2" SS drop pipes to coarse bubble diffusers (detail 1 "coarse bubble mixer": 2" SS drop pipe and tee, 2"×1" reducer at the tee, 1"×3/4" SS reducer, diffuser centerline 2.0' above floor), with a normal operating range marked between EL 25.3 and EL 21.3. The 12" CSBC base is "gravel backfill for foundations, Class 'A' per WSDOT Standard Specifications 9-03.12(1)A" — Unresolved: external reference, not staged.

Summary: Digester alarm set points: high alarm 25.55 on transducer level sensor S1 and low alarm 15.30 on transducer level sensor S2. Section B runs through the digester (top of wall 26.80, high water surface 25.3, T-valve operation range 21.3 to 25.3, bottom EL 14.3 and 13.3, TOC 14.8 and 15.3, slope 3.1%, 30° minimum slope for non-shrink grout) and the UV chamber, showing a 4" telescoping valve "see specifications", the 2" SCH 80 PVC digested sludge line (IE 20.50) on vertical pipe supports per 7/C7.2, the 3" WAS pipe (IE 19.50), the 4" drain pipe (IE 17.25), the 10" effluent pipe (IE 18.75), a "12" D.I. final effluent" label, 8" DI secondary effluent into the 8" influent pipe (IE 19.61), a control panel, concrete supports for the UV equipment (four total), HWL 21.49 and 21.09, handwheels for exposed valves, and 1" SCH 80 PVC drains to a floor drain (IE 16.00). Section C (digester) shows the 4" air pipe (IE 20.0) to coarse bubble diffusers, the 4" telescoping valve on vertical pipe supports per 6/C7.2, a 2" intake for digested sludge (IE 14.80) in a 2.00' square sump, the 4" ductile iron supernatant drain (IE 15.3), the I-beam ("see structural") and an 8.3% floor slope. Section D (UV chamber) shows the two UV units on supports, 4" floor drains (rim EL 18.74), 1" SCH 80 PVC drains for all four drain ports and a 4" ductile iron floor drain (IE 16.00). Summary: Detail 1 shows the Trojan UV disinfection unit: one bank (1A) of "4-64 UV PTP" modules, "6 required / bank" (read at stored resolution; the text layer also carries 6 module label groups), in a steel channel about 13'-7 1/2" long (a 9'-7" module section between 2'-0 3/4" transition boxes, 1'-4" inside channel height) with removable cover plates, module lamp status viewing plates, an access plate with warning label, solid blocking, 2" NPT drains with plugs, a standard 3600K level control weir with a 1" NPT drain plug, and flanged influent and effluent connections drilled to fit 12" DIN, BS and JIS pipe; HWL 21.49 upstream, 21.09 downstream, EL 19.08. Power: a splitter panel within 10 ft of the module power end (120 V, 1-phase, 19.1 A from distribution panel DP, not shown), power distribution receptacles (6.3 A each, from the splitter panel), 10' grounded power cords, and a wall-mounted system monitor within 15 ft of the channel (120 V, 5 A from DP). Notes: do not slope the channel floor; hold channel width and depth to ±1/4"; the contractor supplies all anchor bolts (3/8" [M10], 4 per transition box); electrical requirements cover the Trojan equipment only, with inrush per local code and extra outlets excluded from the interconnect amperage; review all Trojan installation instructions first; do not encase the steel channel in concrete. The module count and "4-64" label do not match G0.7's 8 modules per channel and 2 lamps per module (Issue 13).

Summary: The liquid profile runs from the proposed influent sampling sump (FG 23.65) and the proposed influent & plant drain pump station (8" influent from the STEP collection system, IE 19.50; FG 23.30) through the plant influent flow meter to the proposed 3-way splitter box (HWL 28.0 at 0.77 MGD; bottom elev 26.00). Existing Trains #1 and #2 run at HWL 23.13 (0.257 MGD), NWL 23.09 (0.063 MGD), static 23.05; proposed Train #3 runs at HWL 25.38, NWL 25.34, static 25.30, top of concrete 26.80, with proposed Train #2 and Train #3 flow meters on the inlets. The proposed effluent flow meter feeds proposed UV disinfection channels #1 and #2 (HWL 21.49 at 0.50 MGD per channel; NWL 19.69 at 0.22 MGD per channel), then existing SSMH *1288 (rim 22.89) and 10" and 8" to the 12" outfall; the 100-year flood elevation is 13', and a proposed effluent sample sump is labeled. The solids profile shows proposed WAS pump equipment (pump rate 20–30 gpm), the proposed aerobic digester with a supernatant telescoping valve (TOC 26.80; supernatant to the plant drain P.S.), proposed sludge pump equipment (20–30 gpm), proposed rotary fan press dewatering equipment and the existing screw press, with filtrate to the plant drain P.S. and solids hauled off site.

Document ID: 40 05 71 | Type: Specification section, 2 pages | Discipline: Process-Mechanical | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); no section-level date
Summary: One rising-stem 4" telescoping valve with at least 48" of travel on the aerated digester outlet, as indicated on the plans (¶1.01 A–B p.451). Construction: seamless stainless tube at least 1/8" thick on a stainless lifting bail; stainless companion flange with a neoprene slip-seal gasket at least 1/4" thick (ID 1/8" under the tube OD), 125# drilling to match the riser; handwheel lift at least 12" in diameter with UHMW thrust bearings, a self-locking 304 SS acme stem, a galvanized square-tube torque nut (or vee-keyed shaft) against rotation, and a clear butyrate stem cover with a position indicator in 1/4" increments; 316 SS pedestal on the concrete side wall with six 5/8"×5" stainless wedge anchors (¶2.01 pp.451–452). Basis of design is Waterman TS-2 or equal (¶2.02 p.452); submittals per 01 33 00 are catalog data, fabrication and installation drawings, and O&M information (¶1.02 A p.451); installation follows the manufacturer's instructions and no testing is specified (¶3.01 p.452). The 48" travel matches the 21.3–25.3 T-valve operating range on C5.3 (Inferred check).

Document ID: 46 66 00 | Type: Specification section, 7 pages (body title "Ultraviolet Disinfection Equipment") | Discipline: Process-Mechanical | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); no section-level date
Summary: Two open-channel, gravity-flow, low-pressure high-intensity UV systems, each able to disinfect alone at max day 0.46 MGD, max month 0.22 MGD and minimum 0.03 MGD with TSS up to 30 mg/L, 33–85°F and UVT of at least 50% at 253.7 nm, to 200 FC/100 mL monthly and 400 FC/100 mL weekly geometric means, guaranteed regardless of influent count (¶1.01 A p.502; design criteria pp.502–503). Arrangement: 4 lamps per module, 6 modules per bank, 2 banks, 48 lamps (12 modules), in stainless channels furnished with the system, delivering at least 30,000 µWs/cm² (30 mJ/cm²) at 50% UVT after sleeve, fouling and aging reductions, proven by an independent bioassay to EPA/625/1-86/021, for outdoor installation without shelter (pp.503–504); basis is Trojan UV3000 PTP (base bid), with alternates bid as an Equipment Alternate and needing 500 North American installations, a bioassay and a 5-year guarantee (¶1.03 A p.502; Part 2 A p.504). Construction: 316 SS or quartz in contact with effluent; modules about 68"×20"×2.8", 38 lb, Type 6P, with electronic ballasts, 10-ft 120 V plug cords and LED lamp status; low-pressure slimline hot-cathode lamps warranted 12,000 hours non-prorated; Type 214 quartz sleeves; per-unit effluent channel with drain, module rack and downstream level control weir holding about 12" depth within 1.5" from zero to peak flow; two inlet and two outlet 304 SS transition boxes; a 304 SS maintenance rack; maximum draw 2,100 W at 120 V (pp.505–507).

nodes.note_text: 33 41 00 | Spec section | Civil | Dec. 30, 2022 project manual (cover p.1); Add. 4 p.2 adds ¶2.02 F Trench Drains — Add. 4 governs | Covers new storm sewer pipe, catch basins, roof drains and retaining wall drainage; submittals are catch basins with frames, grates and lids, and storm and roof drain piping and accessories (¶1.01, ¶1.03; main spec p.447 — Verified). Storm pipe is double-wall corrugated polyethylene (ADS N12, Hancor HiQ or equal), ductile iron where cover is under 18 in, and CDF-encased where cover is under 1 ft; roof drains are PVC and wall footing drains are perforated corrugated PE with PVC tight lines (¶2.02 A, ¶3.02 D.7; pp.447–449 — Verified; WSDOT 9-05.20, 9-05.13, 9-05.1(5), 9-05.2(7) Unresolved: external reference, not staged). Type 1 and 1L catch basins, frames, covers and herringbone grates follow WSDOT 9-05.50(3), 9-05.15 and Standard Plans B-5.20-03, B-5.40-02, B-30.10-03, B-30.20-04 and B-30.50-03, installed per WSDOT 7-05.3 with frames on precast grade rings in a full mortar bed (¶2.02 C, ¶3.02 E; pp.448–449 — Verified; Unresolved: external reference, not staged). Add. 4 adds ¶2.02 F: trench drains are Zurn Z886-HD or approved equal, HDPE channels with 0.75% built-in slope, 4-in inside width, 80-in minimum lengths with interlocking ends, black Dura-coated heavy-duty steel frames with embedment studs, and slotted ductile iron grates (5.375 in wide, about 18.5 sq in open area per LF) bolted after final inspection, Load Class C — Add. 4 governs (Add. 4 p.2 — Verified). Footing drain bedding, backfill and construction follow Sections 3.5 and 3.7 of the geotechnical report 'dated September 7, 2021', the Contractor provides construction layout staking, roof drains tight-line to catch basins with 12 in minimum cover, and removed storm sewer is fully removed or plugged (¶2.02 E, ¶3.02 B, F–H; pp.448–450 — Verified; date already flagged, 02 Merge flag 2; staking conflict, see Issues).

Document ID: C6.2 | Type: Drawing — equipment and piping plan | Discipline: Civil (per 01); process-mechanical content | Revision/Date: BID SET; title block NOV 2, 2022; seal 11-02-2022; revision "Ecology Review Comments" JGC 8/9/22; title differs from the cover index ("& VALVING") — cosmetic, already logged in 01 (#8)
Summary: Three 3 HP packaged sludge pumps "per 22 13 36 packaged sludge pump equipment" (keyed note 8) sit side by side against an existing building exterior wall: a WAS pump, a swing pump (standby for either the WAS or the digested sludge pump) and a digested sludge pump. WAS #1, #2 and #3 each enter through an ASCO Redhat series 8221 2" normally closed solenoid valve (catalog 8221G013, 120 V coil, 150 psi max differential, brass body, stainless internals, NEMA 4X; keyed note 1) between 2" PVC manual ball valves (keyed note 7); WAS goes "to digester" in a 2" line carrying a 2" flow meter "per electrical design requirements" between 2" unions (keyed notes 2, 3). Digested sludge comes "from digester" in 4" SCH 80 PVC (keyed note 9) with a 4"×2" reducer, and the digested sludge pump discharges through a 2"×3" expansion "to rotary fan press"; manifold piping is 2" SCH 80 PVC (keyed note 4) on supports per 5/C7.2 (keyed note 5), with the wall annulus filled watertight with Dow Corning 732 sealant (keyed note 6). General note: coordinate piping alignment with the Owner and field configure for best access.
Tags: Equipment — WAS pump, swing pump, digested sludge pump (3 HP each), WAS solenoid valves (3), 2" flow meter, ball valves, unions, sludge manifold piping · Spec sections — 22 13 36 · Sheets — 5/C7.2 · Addenda — Add. 4 p.2, 22 13 36 ¶2.01 A (pump VFDs; applied on the pump rows)
Related documents: G0.5, G0.6, G0.7; C5.1, C5.3 (digester connections); C6.1 (press feed); 22 13 36; Add. 4 p.3 C1.6A item (sludge piping below an existing floor — Civil & Site stack, not read). Issues 17, 18.

nodes.label: Wiki note G0.7
nodes.note_text:
Document ID: G0.7 | Type: Drawing — design criteria tables | Discipline: General (per 01); process content | Revision/Date: BID SET; title block NOV 2, 2022; seal 11-02-2022; revision block not captured
Summary: Start-up design (after Phase I) is ADF 0.10, MMF 0.12, max day 0.30 and peak hour 0.49 MGD; build-out (year 2040, after Phase II — phase numerals read from the image, Verified-Visual) is 0.19, 0.22, 0.46 and 0.77 MGD. The Influent Pump Station has 2 small submersible pumps (120–220 gpm each) and 2 large (320–500 gpm each), firm capacity 535 gpm (0.77 MGD) with one small and one large out of service; electromagnetic flow meters are influent 6" (0–880 gpm), Train #2 and Train #3 8" (0–470 gpm each), effluent 8" (0–940 gpm), plant drain 4" (0–200 gpm) and 2W water 1" (0–25 gpm). Train 3 has one 5 HP submersible mixer in each anoxic zone (#1 15,686 gal, #2 8,789 gal), aeration zone #1 (29,793 gal, 8 diffusers, 192 scfm) and zone #2 (9,889 gal, 2 diffusers, 48 scfm) with "medium bubble" aeration mixing, a RAS airlift (15 scfm, 3", 51 gpm) and a nitrate recycle airlift (61 scfm, 6", 203 gpm), for 316 scfm total at 9.2 psig; clarifiers are 3 units, 18 ft, SWD 13.25' (cells 1–2) and 15.50' (cell 3). UV has 2 lamps per module, 8 modules per channel and 2 channels at 0.5 MGD each, design dose printed "30,000 MJ/CM2" and UVT 50% or greater; the aerobic digester is 15,000 gal with coarse bubble aeration (6 diffusers × 20 cfm) and manual T-valve decant control. WAS and digester pumps are each 1 duty + 1 standby (swing) hose (peristaltic) pumps, 0–40 gpm; one rotary fan press takes 12 gpm at 2% or 20 gpm at 0.5% solids and makes 12–16% cake (up to 1,000 wet / 120 dry lb/hr); 2W water pumps are 1 duty + 1 standby submersible, 20–80 gpm on VFD control.

Document ID: G0.5 | Type: Drawing — process schematic | Discipline: General (per 01, sheet prefix); process content | Revision/Date: BID SET; title block NOV 2, 2022; seal 11-02-2022; revision "Ecology Review Comments" JGC 8/9/22 (triangle reads 6 at stored resolution)
Summary: 8" STEP influent and an influent sample sump feed the Influent Pump Station, which pumps through a 6" influent flow meter to the flow splitter; the splitter feeds Treatment Cell #1 (Train #1) on INF1, Treatment Cell #2 (Train #2) through an 8" Train #2 flow meter on INF2, and New Treatment Cell #3 (Train #3) through an 8" Train #3 flow meter on INF3, with a fourth outlet marked FUTURE. Secondary effluent SE1–SE3 passes an 8" effluent flow meter into UV Channels #1 and #2, then 10" final effluent runs to SSMH *1288 and the 12" outfall; a 4" UV chamber drain is shown. WAS1–WAS3 go to a WAS pump and the aerobic digester above the UV chamber; a digested sludge pump with a flow meter feeds the rotary fan press and the existing screw press (drawn gray), and the 4" pressate drain returns through a 4" plant drain flow meter to the pump station. Train #3 shows Anoxic 1, Anoxic 2, Aeration 1, Aeration 2 and a clarifier, with ML recycle airlift pumps, a RAS airlift pump, and a carbon addition point into Anoxic 2. Legend: isolation valve, flow direction, flow meter (FM), airlift pump.

nodes.label: Wiki note 22 13 36

Document ID: 22 13 36 | Type: Specification section, 2 pages | Discipline: Process-Mechanical | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); ¶2.01 A revised by Add. 4 (February 9, 2023) p.2 — Add. 4 governs
Summary: Furnish and install three sludge pumps — one WAS pump, one digested sludge pump and one swing pump for either service — for dilute sludge at 0.5% to 3.0% solids (¶1.01 A–B p.263). Base ¶2.01 A (p.263) calls for Edson Platinum peristaltic pumps or equal, 3 HP, 460 V, 3-phase, 0 to 43 gpm (typical set point 10 to 30 gpm), corrosion resistant, with a VFD and a local speed dial per pump, an electrical control panel per pump and a 304 SS enclosure of about 40"×40"×40" per pump. Add. 4 p.2 replaces "Each pump is to include a VFD" with: pumps powered from VFDs in the Motor Control Center, VFDs controlled by the PLC in the Main Control Panel, no local speed control dial at the pump, see Electrical Sheets — Add. 4 governs. Controls follow 26 80 00 ¶3.09 A (WAS pump control) and H (rotary fan press system) (¶2.02 p.263); submittals per 01 33 00 are catalog data with wiring diagrams and O&M information (¶1.02 A p.263); the manufacturer furnishes three sets of wear parts (¶2.03 p.263) and provides installation certification, 2 days of start-up and field testing and 1 day of operator training (¶3.02 p.264).

Document ID: C4.2 | Type: Drawing — plan and elevation | Discipline: Civil (per 01); process-mechanical content | Revision/Date: BID SET; title block NOV 2, 2022; seal 11-02-2022; revision block blank
Summary: The plant water (2W) pump station is a 96" diameter precast wet well (floor 10.00', top 21.50', on a 12" crushed surfacing base course) under a 30" fiberglass wet well and access structure (top 0.2' above FG, 23.1'±) with an insulated fiberglass gasketed lid on stainless bolts and a 38" traffic-rated lid and manhole ring per 3/C7.5. 2W water arrives "from air gap, see C4.3" in 4" SCH 80 PVC at 2% slope (4" inlet IE 19.50; Kor-N-Seal or equal at the wall penetration), while the plan view labels a 6" inlet pipe (Issue 39). Two submersible well pumps per specifications (single-pump duty points 20 gpm @ 380' TDH, 72 gpm @ 150' TDH, 80 gpm @ 85' TDH) each discharge through a 2" high-pressure discharge assembly (ball valve, true union ball check valve, high-pressure flex hose, quick disconnect; Orenco or approved equal) set within 12" of the lid, with a pressure relief valve rated 110 psi or greater within 24" of the wet well top, then 2" SCH 80 PVC and a 2"×3" reducer to 3" HDPE; field-fit brackets steady the flow-induced tower assembly. Floats: F1 high level alarm and redundant valve close 22.00, F2 valve close 20.00, F3 valve open 19.00, F4 low level alarm and pumps off 15.00; a 1" PVC vent is tapped into the basin and run to a field-located point out of the vehicle drive path (coordinate with Owner). Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 2 (exterior of all precast concrete wet well joints sealed with CANUSA-CPS WrapidSeal or approved equal) applies to this precast wet well, where C4.2 calls no joint sealant — Add. 4 governs.

Summary: Two air diaphragm tanks, 119 gallons each, "model to be as described in specifications" and configured for the Owner's desired operating pressure range, stand side by side against a wall on a floor at FF 23.30' (TOC 23.30'). Their 1" SCH 80 PVC manifold on 4 floor pipe supports carries pressure transducer PIT-620 (labeled "EQ# PIT-620"; 0–150 psi per specifications; operating pressure 55–75 psi), a 0–150 psi pressure gage with stainless accessories, a pressure relief valve rated 120 psi or greater (Clayton Mark or equal), a 5/8" faucet for air relief and sampling, Simmons S1704 tank tees or equal, 1" ball valves and a pressure-rated end plug. Notes: fill all piping with clean domestic potable water before starting and testing the 2W system equipment; the contractor coordinates the piping connection style (grooved, flanged, threaded) and performs pressure testing to demonstrate watertight construction; valve handles and hoist chains are not shown. The sheet does not name the room; Add. 4 p.3 (A1.1, A1.2, C6.4 item) adjusts "Bladder Tanks" with the Blower Building layout, taken here to be these tanks (Inferred; checked against C6.4 in batch 4).

Document ID: 15 40 00 | Type: Specification section, 2 pages | Discipline: Process-Mechanical (lane per 02, decision D) | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); no section-level date
Summary: Covers miscellaneous plumbing "for exterior purposes only" as described and shown on the plans (¶1.01 A p.253), with shop drawing and product data submittals (¶1.02 A) and compliance with the UBC, UPC and Eastsound Sewer and Water District standards (¶1.03 A). Materials: ABS DWV soil and waste piping above and below ground, unions at equipment connections, full-size cleanouts ("provide brass lugs, with graphite lubricant on threads"), 1" frost-proof yard hydrants (stainless rod and pipe, automatic draining, backflow preventer, 3/4" hose thread, Smith Cooper 0190167II vacuum breaker or equal, 4' bury; Woodford Iowa Y2 or Merrill CV-1000 or equal), and 2" post hydrants (316 SS hardware, 304 SS lower stem rod, hand wheel, brass working parts, 4' bury; American AVK Dry Barrel 67XX or Eclipse No. 2A or equal) with 2" Danfoss AVB atmospheric vacuum breakers (125 psi, ASSE 1001) (¶2.01 A–E p.253). Installation slopes drains 1/4" per foot, provides code cleanouts and follows manufacturer instructions and local codes (¶3.01 p.254); no testing is specified. No sheet in the P&M stack shows hydrant or drain locations or quantities (cross-lane item for Merge).

nodes.label: Wiki note 43 22 10
nodes.note_text:
Document ID: 43 22 10 | Type: Specification section, 4 pages | Discipline: Process-Mechanical | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); ¶2.01 A revised by Add. 4 (February 9, 2023) p.2 — Add. 4 governs
Summary: A complete 2W plant water system: two 2W pumps, pump station accessories, one fiberglass enclosure with a flow meter system, one fiberglass enclosure with an air gap system, two air diaphragm tanks, yard hydrants, wall-mount eye wash stations, and the piping and valving shown (¶1.01 A–B p.472). Base ¶2.01 A (p.472): two ITT Goulds 55GS50 4"-well submersible pumps with stainless components and Centripro M50434 5 HP 460 V 3-phase motors (or equal), 20–80 gpm, "Pumps are to include variable frequency drives (VFDs)", holding a constant user-set pressure (about 50–75 psi) and alternating after each on/off cycle; Add. 4 p.2 replaces the VFD sentence with VFDs in the Motor Control Center controlled by the PLC in the Main Control Panel — Add. 4 governs. Accessories are Orenco SBEX splice boxes, SBCS conduit seals, an MF2 float switch assembly with MFCOLLAR1 collars, HV discharge assemblies (2" with ball valve, check valve, flex hose and quick disconnect per pump), a PB30 pump basin and pressure relief valves each set at 110 psi (Clayton Mark or equal) (¶2.02 A p.473); the tanks are Amtrol Well-X-Trol WX-350D, 119 gal (26" × 62"), with relief valves at 100 psi on the tank tee and 120 psi on the pump discharge piping, a further 120 psi relief valve, a pressure transducer for pump on/off and a 0–150 psi gauge (¶2.03 A p.473; Issue 26). Exposed plant water pipe gets 1.25" closed-cell polyisocyanurate insulation (Trymer 2000 XP or equal) under a 26-gauge aluminum jacket, and exposed plant water piping, hydrants and pump discharge piping are labeled and painted per "Section 09 91 00" and Divisions 9 and 33, stainless pipe excepted (¶2.04–2.05 pp.473–474; Issue 27).

nodes.label: Wiki note 00 31 13
nodes.note_text:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | 00 31 13 |
| Type | Spec section — Bidding Requirements (Part 1): preliminary phasing plan and milestone dates |
| Discipline | General |
| Revision/Date | Project manual Dec. 30, 2022 (main spec cover p.1, per 00 register). Body title reads "Preliminary Project Phases" (p.21; wording only) |
| Summary | The phasing plan is for planning only and does not dictate means and methods (p.21; Verified). San Juan County building permit applications were submitted Nov 2021 with approvals June 2022; bid phase: advertise Jan 4, pre-bid Jan 18, open bids Feb 8, award Feb 15, preconstruction meeting Mar 15, 2023 (p.21; Verified). Construction starts with submittals after award (long-lead items first) and March 2023 mobilization, a temporary bypass pipe per the Plan of Interim Operation (April 2023), then Blower Building, digester, UV disinfection chamber, sludge pumps, yard piping, vaults and electrical (April 2023), the 2W air gap water system (May 2023), influent pump station (June 2023) and Train 3 (August 2023) (¶A.1–10, p.21; Verified). A temporary 480V generator is rented from Sept 25, 2023 until the permanent 480V generator is installed, tested and on line in April 2024, and the new 480V service, MCC and PLC panel complete Oct 4, 2023 (¶A.11–12, p.21; ¶A.21, p.22; Verified). Milestones: major piping Nov 1, 2023; dewatering system Feb 9, 2024; Train 3 complete July 8, 2024 then seeded with 10,000 gal of activated sludge July 8–12; Substantial Completion July 26, 2024; Final Completion Oct 16, 2024 (¶A.18–27, p.22; Verified).

| Summary | Thirty-five Supplemental Conditions modify the WSDOT Standard Specifications (2022 Ed.), which serve as the base conditions (Unresolved: external reference, not staged); precedence runs Change Orders, Contract Form, Addenda, permits, Drawings, Supplemental Conditions, Technical Specifications, District standards, WSDOT drawings, WSDOT specs (SC 1–2, 5, pp.88–89; Verified); the 00 53 00 and 00 54 00 funding inserts are not placed in that order (Issues 2.7). The Contractor stakes the work, picks up the District Land Disturbance permit and San Juan County Building Permit #21-0385 (stated as still in process), gives 48-hour utility and connection notices, works 7AM–5PM Mon–Fri with $150/hr inspection charge past 40 hr/week, and self-performs at least 50% of the contract price (SC 7–14, pp.89–91; Verified; permit status conflicts with 00 31 13 — Issues 1.9). SC 15 sets completion by Oct. 16, 2024 within 360 working days on site; SC 16 requires the CPM schedule at the pre-construction meeting and the Schedule of Values within 10 working days of NTP; SC 17 holds 5% retainage; SC 18 sets liquidated damages per working day as LD = 0.15C/T per WSDOT 1-08.9 (pp.91–92; Verified; WSDOT part Unresolved: external reference, not staged; basis conflicts with 00 41 00 — Issues 1.8).

nodes.label: Wiki note 01 45 00
nodes.note_text:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | 01 45 00 |
| Type | Spec section — Division 01 General Requirements (Part 3) |
| Discipline | General |
| Revision/Date | Project manual Dec. 30, 2022 (main spec cover p.1, per 00 register); no section-level date |
| Summary | Splits inspection and testing between the parties: the Contractor keeps records of all inspections and tests, pays for repeat tests after any failure (including Owner-responsibility tests), gives 48 hours' notice before work needing inspection, and uses only Owner-approved laboratories (¶1.05.A–E, ¶1.06.C, pp.137–139; Verified). Contractor-paid: pipe pressure testing and potable water pipe disinfection per the technical sections, equipment testing per the equipment sections (Division 46, p.141), clean water leakage testing, and clean water mechanical testing of pumps, diffusers, mixers and air lift assemblies (¶1.05.B.1, p.137; Verified). Owner-paid, Contractor-coordinated: building special inspections for concrete and structural steel (the p.141 summary adds air barrier testing per WA Energy Code Section 402), earthwork, concrete, asphalt (Rice density, compaction, extraction/gradation), coatings and field welding (¶1.05.B.2, pp.137–138, p.141; Verified); the WSDOT/AASHTO compaction and asphalt testing standards (¶1.03.B, p.136) are Unresolved: external reference, not staged. Before startup, eight new structures get a fill-to-rim clean water leakage test held 2 hours with no visible leakage — influent pump station, flow splitter, aeration basins, anoxic basins, clarifier, UV disinfection chamber, digester, 2W water system pump station (¶1.09, pp.139–140; Verified; repeated in 01 50 00 — Issues 1.22). The Owner's on-site representative cannot change the contract or accept work, and missed defects can still be rejected later (¶1.07–1.08, p.139; Verified).

nodes.label: Wiki note 01 50 00
nodes.note_text:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | 01 50 00 |
| Type | Spec section — Division 01 General Requirements (Part 3) |
| Discipline | General |
| Revision/Date | Project manual Dec. 30, 2022 (main spec cover p.1, per 00 register); no section-level date |
| Summary | The Contractor arranges all temporary utilities; a field office is encouraged but not required, while water and sanitation must be provided for all workers (¶1.01.A–B, p.142; Verified; field office conflicts with 01 31 00 — Issues 1.16). Required facilities: temporary power and lighting to the closest utility source, metered construction water with backflow prevention if agreed, temporary restrooms, drinking water, protected storage, first aid per WAC 296-24, and access at all times to homes, the WWTP and water treatment plant, and the helicopter pad for emergency vehicles (¶1.04.A–G, I, pp.142–144; Verified). Wastewater bypass systems are required for both influent and effluent; bypass pumping and other temporary process equipment need continuous oversight by on-site staff or an alarm with automatic cellular notification, 24/7 call-out with on-site response within 30 minutes, and backup alarms and running status wired to the District's existing control system, with PLC/SCADA programming incidental (¶1.01.D.2, ¶1.04.H, pp.142–144; Verified). The clean water leakage test repeats 01 45 00 but groups the aeration basins, anoxic basins and clarifier under Train #3 and names UV channels #1 and #2 and the 2W pump station wet well (¶1.04.C, p.143; Verified; Issues 1.22). Cleanup, noise, dust, erosion control per 31 32 11, pollution control and barriers at all hazards close the section (¶1.05–1.08, pp.144–145; Verified; barrier text repeats 00 73 00 SC 23), and temporary items come out at completion of the work (¶1.01.C, ¶1.04.A.4, ¶1.04.B.3, ¶1.04.D.1; removal timing conflicts with 01 70 00 — Issues 1.19).

| Discipline | General |
| Revision/Date | December 1, 2022; Wilson Engineering Project # 2020-070 (p.1) |
| Summary | Wilson Engineering's plan, prepared under WAC 173-240-075, for documenting that construction meets the contract plans and specifications; it says it is not part of the Contract Documents, so the contract governs wherever the two differ (§1.0–1.3, pp.4–5; Verified; WAC and WSDOT 2022 texts Unresolved: external reference, not staged). The District (General Manager Jason Bradshaw) funds the work, approves pay requests and changes, inspects daily and must keep treatment uninterrupted; Wilson (Project Engineer Jeff Christner, PE; Inspector Sam Rodriguez; subconsultants Ztek electrical, GeoEngineers geotechnical, Kingworks structural) performs CQA, submittal review, record drawings and the plant O&M manual; the WA-licensed Contractor owns quality control (§4, pp.6–9; Fig. 4-1 p.23; Verified; rule citations — Issues 2.10). Wilson observes on site at least 1 day per week and keeps daily reports, a weekly working-day tally, photos and quantity records, and the plan expects a Contractor field office to hold the schedule, photos, pay requests, test records, RFI/Work Directive/Change Order files and reviewed submittals (§5, §8, pp.10–12, p.18; Verified; field office — Issues 1.16).

Summary: The material list names one each of: rotary press model (steel), flocculator (steel), sludge manifold and piping (316 SS), cake chute (LLDPE), air compressor and control panel, all "Section 46 76 26"; an emulsion polymer make-up system, "Section 46 33 33"; and screw conveyor equipment (SS), "Section 46 12 13" (not a section in the spec — Issue 14). The plan (press line about 161" [13'-5"] by 84 3/4" [7'-0 3/4"], conveyor 131 11/16" [10'-11 11/16"]) shows the press, flocculator, sludge manifold, operator interface, control panel, a 30"×30" "dry polymer mix unit" (Issue 16), 3" digested sludge in, 2" 2W water, and 4" pressate out "to influent pump station". The elevation shows the screw conveyor rising at 28° over 147 15/16" [12'-3 15/16"] to discharge at 90" [7'-6"] into a mobile dumpster for sludge cake collection (40" [3'-4"] high), with the 2W water supply pipe, 3" digester sludge and 4" pressate drain pipe below the floor.

nodes.label: Wiki note 41 12 13
nodes.note_text:
Document ID: 41 12 13 | Type: Specification section, 9 pages | Discipline: Process-Mechanical | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); no section-level date
Summary: One complete screw conveyor system carries dewatered cake "from the rotary presses" to the final discharge point, with drives, motors, instrumentation, controls and supports, designed by the manufacturer to CEMA, AGMA, AWS D1.1 and AISC standards (¶1.1–1.2, ¶1.5 pp.453–455). The schedule (pp.460–461) lists two units: a "Receiving Conveyor" (horizontal, shaftless, 9" flight at 9" pitch, 6'-9" long, 304 SS U-trough 11 ga, two inlets from rotary press cake chutes, outlet to the inclined conveyor, Nord SK2282 SCP, 1 HP, 24 rpm) and an "Inclined Conveyor" (shafted, 9" flight at 5" pitch, 17'-4" long at 35°, 304 SS tubular O-trough 10 ga, outlet to bin, Nord SK2282 SCP, 5 HP, 53 rpm), both 0.5 wet ton/hr at 45% loading and 45 lb/ft³, with 3/8" UHMW liners and 2" drains. Troughs follow CEMA 300 in sections of 8 ft max, with UHMW wear liners in 4-ft pieces, a 2" stainless ball drain valve, anti-flotation devices every 16 ft on shaftless units and saddle supports at 16 ft max; drives are TEFC inverter-duty 1800 rpm motors on Nord shaft-mount reducers (AGMA Class 11, 1.4 service factor), with Siemens Sitrans WM100 zero-speed switches (120 VAC, NEMA 4X) wired to the PLC and interlocked with the MCC starter, and the conveyors run from the rotary press PLC and operator interface (¶1.8–1.13 pp.456–459). Submittals cite "Section 01340" and "Section 01 30 00" and repeat telescoping valve wording (¶1.3 A p.454; Issue 23), plus data sheets and component lists (¶1.3 B); each conveyor is shop assembled and run before shipment (¶3.02 A p.460). The two-conveyor, two-inlet arrangement does not match C6.1's single 28° conveyor from one press (Issue 22); Part 2 numbering runs 1.6–1.13 as printed.

Document ID: 46 33 33 | Type: Specification section, 5 pages | Discipline: Process-Mechanical | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); no section-level date
Summary: One fully operational emulsion (liquid) polymer make-up system that activates and blends neat polymer (40–55% active) into a homogeneous 0.1–0.5% solution (¶1.01 A p.481). Components: a water pressure reducing valve set to 40 psi (supply 45–100 psi) with gauge; a proportional dilution-water valve (ball valve and positioner needing at least 90 psi air; flow "0.1 to 20 GPM (0.4 to 75 LPH)" as printed — Issue 29) regulated on the polymer-to-sludge ratio from the Rotary Press PLC, using the flow meter on the flocculator supplied with the press; a peristaltic metering pump (0.1–500 mL/min, up to 7 bar) with an inlet strainer; and a static mixer, on a 304 SS frame with HDPE water piping (Part 2 items 2.1–2.5 pp.481–482). Electrical: a 24 VDC, 4–20 mA proportional valve, a 120 VAC or 24 VDC pump with 4–20 mA control, and a NEMA 4X junction box with a 120 VAC/24 VDC supply, powered from a 120 VAC outlet or the Fournier control panel and run from the Rotary Press PLC and HMI in hand or auto (items 3.0–4.0 p.482). The materials list names Fournier Industries (frame, brackets), Watson-Marlow (dosing pump), Koflo (static mixer), Watts (regulator), Festo (proportional valve), Hoffman (10×10×8 junction box) and McMaster (valves, strainer, gauges, hose), with one metering pump head kit as the spare (items 6.0–7.0 pp.482–483); p.484 carries no text. Submittals cite "Section 01340" with telescoping-valve wording (¶1.02 A p.481; Issue 29), installation follows the manufacturer's instructions with no testing specified (¶3.01 p.485), and the liquid system conflicts with C6.1's "dry polymer mix unit" label (Issue 16).

nodes.label: Wiki note 46 76 26
nodes.note_text:
Document ID: 46 76 26 | Type: Specification section, 22 pages | Discipline: Process-Mechanical | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); no section-level date
Summary: A single-source, shop-tested "plug and play" dewatering skid: one rotary fan press with one 36" dewatering channel, a flocculator, sludge manifold and piping, cake chute, an emulsified-polymer make-up system with dosing pump, an air compressor for pneumatic valving, screw conveyors (receiving and inclined "as needed" to reach the District's dumpster, as shown on drawings) and one control panel for the whole system, which also sets the digested sludge feed pump rate (¶1.0 A, C p.510; ¶1.7 p.514). Duty: at least 120 dry lb/hr from 0.5–2.5% solids at 5–25 gpm, producing 12–16% cake and up to 1,000 wet lb/hr, with design runtimes of 4.6–35.0 hours per week across current and 2040 cases (¶1.0 B, D, E pp.510–511); the press has a 1.5 HP 480 V TEFC drive, stainless hard-chrome filtration elements, six scrapers, a wash system limited to 750 gallons per 2.5 hours because "the 2W (air gap) water system has limited capacity", an LLDPE filtrate collector (7.5" outlet) to a 6" Sch 80 PVC manifold and LLDPE cake chutes (¶1.1–1.4 pp.512–514). The flocculator (model 05-300-900, 17 gal, 100 psi) has a 1 HP Nord SK0282 variable-speed agitator and a PVC air breather tied to "the potable water line", feeding the press through Sch 10 316 SS piping with Victaulic joints, 3" pneumatic feed and recirculation ball valves, lever channel isolating valves, 1" pneumatic wash valves and a 1" stainless polymer check valve, with the feed manifold shop tested at 100 psi (¶2.1–2.2 pp.515–518).

31 23 19 | Spec section | Civil | Dec. 30, 2022 project manual (cover p.1); no addendum item | Covers dewatering of all excavations until backfill reaches finished grade (¶1.1; main spec p.389 — Verified). Submittal: a dewatering plan before construction, 'in accordance with Section 01 30 00', showing methods, equipment, well and sump details, stormwater diversions, discharge points and contingency plans for settlement; it is kept up to date like the TESC plan (¶1.2; p.389 — Verified; section number not in the manual, see Issues). Groundwater was monitored for ten months (Appendix B) and much higher levels are expected in winter; the section also cites the 'September 7, 2021' geotechnical report (¶1.3–1.4; p.390 — Verified; date already flagged, 02 Merge flag 2). The Contractor keeps backup pumps and a standby generator on site, dewaters at least 2 ft below any structure base, builds wells to WAC 173-160, and may not discharge to the sanitary sewer, outfall or WWTP (Part 2, ¶3.1–3.2; pp.390–391 — Verified). Testing: discharge is checked with a Rossum sand tester (10 ppm silica maximum) with 24-hour notice, and settlement reference points are observed near critical structures (¶3.2–3.3; pp.391–392 — Verified). | Equipment: Dewatering system (pumps, backup pumps, standby generator, wells); Spec sections: 01 30 00 (cited; not in manual); Appendices B, C; Sheets: —; Addenda: — | Appendix B; Appendix C; 31 20 00; 31 32 11; C0.2 (Element 10)
