nodes.note_text: C0.2 | Drawing sheet — temporary erosion and sediment control narrative | Civil | BID SET; title block NOV 2, 2022; seal 11-02-2022 (Verified); revision 1 'Ecology Review Comments' JGC 8/9/22 (Verified-Visual) | Construction stormwater narrative organized by the 13 required elements (clearing limits, construction access, flow rates, sediment controls, soil stabilization, slopes, drain inlets, channels and outlets, pollutants, dewatering, BMP maintenance, project management, low-impact-development BMPs) plus general notes on BMP installation, maintenance and removal (plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual). Project description: total project area 0.45 ac, proposed impervious area 0.04 ac, area to be disturbed 0.30 ac, estimated cut 3,382 CY and fill 1,596 CY, stated as for the TESC narrative only and not for bidding or take-off (Item 15; plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual). The site is mostly flat, with grass turf along the north and south property lines and no trees or shrubs; runoff flows southeast to northwest into a ditch on the adjoining site along the north boundary; there are no streams, lakes, wetlands, residential or critical areas; soils are mapped as Roche-Killebrew complex, 2 to 10 percent slopes (Items 16–21; plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual). Sequence: install silt fence, construction entrance and inlet protection; remove pavement for sewer structures; clear and grade for the building addition and retaining wall; build them; install stormwater conveyance; pave and stabilize landscape areas (Item 22; plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual). Construction is expected from spring 2023 to fall 2024; no sediment ponds, diversions or waterways are used and no detention calculations are needed (Items 23–24; plans_2Part-1 p.1, C0.2 — Verified-Visual).

| Summary | Gives general submittal procedures and a non-exhaustive checklist; item-specific requirements sit in the individual sections (¶1.01, ¶1.03, p.129; Verified). The checklist's bid-phase entries cite sections and attachments that do not exist in the project manual — 00 43 36, 00 22 13, 00 45 14, and DBE forms as "Attachments 6 and 7" of 00 73 00 — and move Contractor Qualifications to 24 hours after opening (¶1.03.A–C, p.129; Issues 1.14, 2.2, 2.5). Before the Agreement: bonds, insurance certificates, prevailing wage filings; 10 days after execution: construction schedule, substitution requests, Schedule of Values; monthly: pay application and updated schedule; certified payroll; 14 days before any WWTP shutdown: a bypass pumping and emergency response plan; closeout: affidavits, record drawings (¶1.03.D–J, pp.129–130; Verified). Submittals are PDF with a transmittal, stamped by the Contractor, with an approved-submittal file kept on site; samples in pairs, product certificates in triplicate, test reports 3 copies (¶1.04–1.05, pp.130–131; Verified). O&M manuals (4 hard, 2 PDF sets) go in draft with shop drawings, final draft before the 75% pay application, and complete before payment above 90% (¶1.05.G, pp.131–132; Verified). |

| Field | Value |

| Type | Spec section — Division 01 General Requirements (Part 3) |
| Discipline | General |
| Revision/Date | Project manual Dec. 30, 2022 (main spec cover p.1, per 00 register); no section-level date |
| Summary | Before requesting Substantial Completion the Contractor delivers tools, spare parts and extra stock, changes over locks and hands over keys, completes start-up testing and operator instruction, removes temporary facilities, turns over record information, finishes cleanup, and provides O&M manuals for all equipment, controls, telemetry and SCADA plus 2015 WSEC compliance documentation per C103.6.3 (¶1.03.A, pp.152–153; Verified; temporary facility removal conflicts with 00 73 00 SC 19 — Issues 1.19; energy code edition — Issues 1.20). The request carries a completion notice, incomplete-items list, pay request, change accounting, warranties and bonds, releases and occupancy/operating certificates, and record documents; "substantially complete" is defined by the WSDOT General Specifications and "Sections 00 72 00 and 00 73 00a" (¶1.03.B, p.153; WSDOT part Unresolved: external reference, not staged; section numbers — Issues 2.5), and warranties start on the Date of Substantial Completion (¶1.03.D.1, p.153; Verified; bears on Issues 1.11). Retainage is released only against an affidavit of paid payrolls and bills, lien releases, the DOR tax form, the L&I affidavit of wages paid and the ESD release (¶1.05.B, p.154; Verified). All mechanical and electrical equipment is tested before any facility goes into operation: procedures due 14 days before start-up covering every control device, equipment item and control circuit, joint sign-off forms, testing witnessed by the Engineer, and manufacturers' representatives who train Owner staff and certify each installation by letter (¶1.06, p.155; Verified).

nodes.note_text:
- **Document ID:** 09 97 23
- **Type:** Specification section — Division 09
- **Discipline:** Architectural
- **Revision/Date:** Main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (00 register: cover p.1, Engineer's Statement seal p.3); no revision marks on the section pages; no Add. 4 item [main spec pp.236–241 — Verified].
- **Summary:** Covers a spray-applied, monolithic, high-build 100%-solids epoxy lining on all interior concrete surfaces of the listed structure — the Influent Pump Station, with detailed locations per the drawings [¶1.01 A–B, p.236 — Verified]. Submittals are product data with ASTM results, MSDS, project guidelines and applicator qualifications (manufacturer certification, trained equipment operators, 5 references, permits) [¶1.02 A, p.236 — Verified]. The product is Raven 405 or Tnemec G436 PermaShield (amine-cured, light green), applied by a certified applicator with heated plural-component spray on concrete cured at least 28 days and blasted to CSP 3–5, at 80 mils min. and 100 mils average wet film [¶2.01 A, ¶2.04 A, ¶2.05, ¶3.03 E, ¶3.05 D, pp.237–239 — Verified]. Testing covers wet-film readings (ASTM D4414), optional ultrasonic dry-film checks (SSPC-PA 9), high-voltage holiday testing at 100 V/mil (NACE RP0188 or ASTM D4787), and pull-off adhesion (ASTM D7234) with 2 of 3 pulls over 200 psi per test area, all documented to the Owner [¶3.06 A–D, pp.239–241 — Verified].
- **Tags:** Items: Influent Pump Station interior concrete epoxy lining · Spec: 03 40 00 (Influent Pump Station precast) · Sheets: cross-lane C4.1 · Addenda: none
- **Related documents:** 03 40 00; cross-lane C4.1 (Process & Mechanical)

Document ID: C3.2 | Type: Drawing — plan, sections and keyed notes | Discipline: Civil (per 01); process-mechanical content | Revision/Date: BID SET; title block NOV 2, 2022; seal 11-02-2022; revision block blank
Summary: Keyed note 7 makes the flow splitter a prefabricated 316 SS unit sized to match the drawing, with 4 equal splitter chambers (flow to each of the 3 trains and 1 additional train), an adjustable weir in each chamber and a removable cover; manufacturer Smith & Loveless or approved equal. The box is about 7'-0" × 4'-6" in plan (outlet spacing 5'-3") with its bottom at elev 26.00 on a proposed concrete support about 6.5' × 4.0' × 1.3' tall; the contractor coordinates the support with the actual box, top of concrete elev 26.00, see structural drawings (keyed note 2); the existing slab TOC is 24.7. The inlet is 6" DI restrained pipe and a restrained 90° bend (INV 20.75) rising through a 12"×6" DI eccentric reducer, 12" DI flange spools and 90° bends on 12" pipe supports per 5/C7.2; outlets are 8" DI flanged bends and spools (one at INV 20.75) on 8" pipe supports per 5/C7.2, labeled To Cell #1, #2 and #3, with a future connection sealed by a blind flange (keyed note 1). A manually adjustable weir is configured to fine-tune an even split among all four outlet pipes.
Tags: Equipment — flow splitter box (316 SS, 4 chambers, adjustable weirs, removable cover), splitter concrete support, 6"/12" DI inlet piping, 8" DI outlets · Spec sections — none printed · Sheets — detail 5/C7.2; "see structural drawings" · Addenda — none

Document ID: C4.1 | Type: Drawing — plan, elevation, keyed notes and control levels | Discipline: Civil (per 01); process-mechanical content | Revision/Date: BID SET; title block NOV 2, 2022; seal 11-02-2022; revision "Ecology Review Comments" JGC 8/9/22
Summary: The new Influent Pump Station is a 96" precast wet well "per WSDOT Std Plan B-15.60-00 for precast manholes" (Unresolved: external reference, not staged) on a 12" thick precast base, interior bottom elev 9.0 and top elev 23.30, with the top slab per 1/S2.4 and 2/S2.4, a 36"×36" Halliday H1R3636 hatch and a 30"×48" Halliday H1R3048 hatch over the pumps (both H-20), and "WrapidSeal or equal" at all joints; it takes 8" influent at IE 19.50, 4" filtrate and digester supernatant at IE 13.40 and a 4" sample sump line at IE 18.00. Small and large pumps, each a duplex arrangement per specs (keyed notes 28, 52, 53), hang on stainless guide rails with stainless haul chains, manufacturer's disconnect elbows and flapper valves that close and seal when submerged; discharges pass through two precast valve vaults (4'-2" × 4'-2" × 5'-6" minimum inside, Utility Vault Co. 506-LA or equal, floor elev 18.0±) with 4" and 6" check and gate valves and pressure gages, into 4" and 6" DI restrained piping with buried gate valves. Floats F1–F4 on timer control start the redundant large lag (19.00), large lead (18.50), small lag (18.00) and small lead (17.50) pumps; the transducer, set 6" above the floor, runs T1 high level alarm 17.50 (with float), T2 large lag 17.00, T3 large lead 16.00, T4 small lag 14.00, T5 small lead 12.00, T6 pumps off 11.00 and T7 low level alarm and redundant off 10.50.

Document ID: C3.1 | Type: Drawing — site plan | Discipline: Civil (per 01, sheet prefix); process piping content | Revision/Date: BID SET; title block NOV 2, 2022; seal 11-02-2022; revision "Ecology Review Comments" JGC 8/9/22
Summary: Plan of the new flow splitter box beside existing Train #1, with 8" outlets to Train #1 (west), Train #2 and Train #3 (south), a future Train #4 connection sealed with an 8" blind flange (keyed note 1), and the inlet from the north; dashed vaults with flow meter symbols sit on the inlet line and on the Train #2 and Train #3 lines, and a vault drain is labeled. Keyed notes: proposed concrete support for the splitter box (2); existing sampling port (3); pipe supports per 5/C7.2 (4); carefully cut a hole through the building for the new 8" Train #1 influent and seal with flashing (5); 8" Train #1 influent elbow discharging into the aeration basin beside the existing influent pipe (7); confirm the existing Train #2 influent pipe and connect new 8" DI piping with positive drainage from the splitter box (8); pot-hole existing 8" piping before construction (9). Construction sequence: install the new splitter box and piping to Trains #1 and #3 without disturbing existing piping and operations; when complete and tested, connect the 8" influent to the new influent pump station and direct flow to Trains #1 and #3; then dewater, abandon and remove existing influent piping conflicts so the Train #2 piping and flow meter vault can be installed. Train #2 downtime is limited to 5 days max (Monday–Friday).

Document ID: 22 13 29 | Type: Specification section, 8 pages | Discipline: Process-Mechanical | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); running header misspells the title ("SUMBERSIBLE") — already logged in 02 (#7)
Summary: A performance specification for the complete, tested Influent Pump Station — pumps, controls, discharge piping, vaults, flow meter and connection to existing piping — with the contractor responsible for field measurements and supplier coordination (¶1.01 A–E p.255). Pump schedule (¶2.02 B p.258): two small pumps, Flygt N3085 MT, 150 gpm @ 20.5 ft design (120 gpm @ 22.0 ft; 220 gpm @ 17.5 ft; shutoff 26 ft), 2.7 HP, 1800 rpm, 43% minimum efficiency, 135 mm Adaptive N-impeller, 3 1/8" discharge; two large pumps, Flygt N3102 MT, 385 gpm @ 20.5 ft (320 gpm @ 22.5 ft; 500 gpm @ 15.0 ft; shutoff 38 ft), 5.0 HP, 1800 rpm, 66%, 152 mm impeller, 3 15/16" discharge; all 460 V 3-phase, rated Class 1 Division 1 Groups C and D, one manufacturer for all (¶2.01 C; ¶2.02 C.1, C.9 pp.257–260). Each pump has a cast-iron discharge connection with a machined metal-to-metal seal, two 316 SS guide bars about 15 ft long (contractor to verify), 316 SS brackets and a 20 ft stainless lifting chain with spectra cord for a Grip-Eye device, three 316 SS cable holders, a Flygt MiniCAS-120 motor saver relay supplied to the Control Systems Integrator, and pressure gages (Marsh P0142, 0–25 psi) with Branom diaphragm isolators and Apollo shutoff valves (¶2.02 C.2, C.10, F; ¶2.03; ¶2.04 pp.259–261).

Document ID: 45 05 00 | Type: Specification section, 5 pages | Discipline: Process-Mechanical | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); no section-level date
Summary: Covers furnishing and installing the valves in the plant piping systems, complete with operators, with submittals per 01 33 00 and NSF 61 materials for potable water (¶1.01–2.01 p.476). Operators open counterclockwise; buried valves take AWWA C504 2" square nuts 18–24" below grade in two-piece cast-iron screw-type valve boxes (Mueller H-10364 or Clow F-2452 or equal) unless in a vault; gear operators keep handwheel pull at 40 lb or less, and butterfly operators show disc position (¶2.02–2.03 pp.476–477). Products: Kennedy resilient-seated NRS gate valves 2"–12" (AWWA C509/C515, C550 epoxy) and all-stainless NPT gate valves under 4" exposed; swing check valves with external lever, spring and limit switch (MH 259-02ALS, AWWA C508) and Tideflex TF-2M duckbill checks for vertical service; Pratt Ballcentric plug valves; Watts S-FBV-1 stainless ball valves under 4" for general exposed non-potable use and Asahi Type 21 CPVC true-union ball valves 2" and under for interior potable water; M&H Style 47 flap gates, demonstrated in dry and wet tests; butterfly valves — Asahi Type 57 PVC for interior PVC systems, Bray Series 31 lug or Dezurik for exposed ductile iron or stainless air piping, AWWA C504 Class 150B for buried water mains 10" and larger; A.R.I. D-025 combination air release valves; 2"-and-under globe valves (Issue 28); and Kennedy gate valves for buried plant water hydrant isolation (¶2.04–2.014 pp.477–479). Every shut-off or control valve gets a 1-1/2" stainless tag with its ID "as listed on the valve schedule", a submitted valve directory, and a label marker in a concrete pad per the plans and valve schedule (¶2.015–2.016 p.479); no valve schedule is in the P&M stack (cross-lane item).

nodes.note_text:
- **Document ID:** S2.4
- **Type:** Drawing — structural plan and sections for the drain pump station lid; generator slab and flow splitter pad details
- **Discipline:** Structural (Kingworks)
- **Revision/Date:** Title block 10-15-2021; revision 2 "Bid Set" TH 9/6/22 [plans_8 p.4 — Verified-Visual]. No Add. 4 drawing entry; Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 2 (precast joint sealant) applies to the wet well joints.
- **Summary:** The drain pump station lid is a 16"-thick cast-in-place concrete lid over an 8' min., 96" I.D. precast wet well (lid diameter to match the wet well O.D.), designed for H-20 truck loading, with two hatches per civil at 2'-6" × 4'-0" rough openings and a center beam between them [plans_8 p.4, S2.4 Detail 1 and Notes 1–6 — Verified-Visual]. Lid bars are placed in a set order (E/W bottom, N/S bottom, N/S top, E/W top) with 1-1/2" clear, the center beam has (2) #8 top and bottom continuous with #4 closed ties @ 3" o.c. max., and the lid keys into the precast wall with joints to be "seal AA at joints per civil" [plans_8 p.4, Details 1–3 — Verified-Visual]. Add. 4 requires the exterior of all precast concrete wet well and vault joints to be sealed with CANUSA-CPS WrapidSeal (manhole encapsulation system) or approved equal, installed per the manufacturer [Add. 4 p.1, Clarification 2 — Verified; Add. 4 governs]. The generator sits on a 6" slab-on-grade (#4 @ 18" o.c. each way, mid-depth) with a thickened edge about 1'-6" min. deep and (2) #4 continuous; the generator itself is "per civil, attachment by others" and is not identified as permanent or temporary [plans_8 p.4, Detail 4 — Verified-Visual; identity — Unresolved, Issues, Missing information #5].

- **Document ID:** 03 40 00
- **Type:** Specification section — Division 03
- **Discipline:** Structural
- **Revision/Date:** Main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (00 register: cover p.1, Engineer's Statement seal p.3); no revision marks on the section pages. Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 2 extends exterior joint sealing to all precast wet well and vault joints — Add. 4 governs [main spec pp.181–185; Add. 4 p.1 — Verified].
- **Summary:** Covers design, supply and installation of all precast concrete structures shown — vaults, top slabs and "the effluent wet well" — with WA-engineer-sealed shop drawings and calculations, mix designs 15 days ahead, material certificates, 5 years of NPCA certification, and Owner/Engineer plant inspection rights [¶1.01 A, p.181; ¶1.06 A–F, ¶1.07, p.182 — Verified; WSDOT M41-10 references ¶1.04 C and ¶1.05 B — Unresolved: external reference, not staged]. Wet wells and vaults are 5,000 psi with A615 Gr 60 rebar to ACI 318-14 and ASTM C857: 96" Oldcastle wet wells with 48"×30" H-20 aluminum hatches (LW Products HD-3C) at the 2W Plant Water Pump Station (C4.2) and Influent Pump Station (C4.1), and 4'×4' Oldcastle 4686-LA vaults with 36"×36" H-20 single-leaf hatches (Halliday H1R3636) for the Influent and Effluent Flow Meter Valve Vaults and Plants 2 & 3 Flow Meter Vault (C7.4) and the Influent Pump Station Meter Vaults (C4.1) [¶2.02 E, p.183 — Verified]. The top slab schedule separately calls for the Influent Pump Station top slab per the Contract Plan details with a new 3'-0"×5'-0" light-duty aluminum hatch with safety grates (Flygt FLED-13 or equal), which conflicts with the 48"×30" H-20 hatch in the vault table [¶2.02 D.1 and E.2, p.183 — Verified; Unresolved — Issues, Conflicts].

nodes.note_text:
31 20 00 | Spec section | Civil | Dec. 30, 2022 project manual (cover p.1); geotech report date already flagged (02 Merge flag 2) | Covers excavation, hauling, disposal, backfill, compaction and final grading; cites the 'September 7, 2021' GeoEngineers report as Appendix C (¶1.01; main spec p.383 — Verified; date conflict already flagged, 02 Merge flag 2). Submittals: gradation and moisture-density curves for imported materials, separation geotextile data, and proposed compaction equipment; field density testing is by the Engineer's independent lab (one test per 100 LF of roadway, 1,000 SF of subgrade, 500 CY of structural backfill), with Contractor-paid retests (¶1.02–1.03; pp.383–384 — Verified). Crushed surfacing base course goes under all slabs and foundations: 12 in minimum for mat foundations and vaults, 18 in for shallow foundations, 24 in for pile structures (¶3.01 D; p.386 — Verified). Structural fill is placed in 10-in loose lifts and compacted to 95% MDD (ASTM D1557); unsuitable subgrade is over-excavated 18 in and replaced with CSBC on written authorization, with haul receipts to the Owner (¶3.03, ¶3.05–3.06; pp.387–388 — Verified). All fill materials are specified by WSDOT section (9-03.9(3), 9-03.10, 9-03.12, 9-03.14, 9-03.19 and others), and dewatering and boulder excavation are incidental (¶2.01, ¶1.04 B; pp.384–386 — Verified; material gradations Unresolved: external reference, not staged). | Equipment: —; Spec sections: 01 33 00; 31 23 19; Appendix C; Sheets: Grading and erosion control plans (cited); Addenda: — | Appendix C; Appendix B; 31 23 19; 31 23 33; 04 Items 10–16

Excavation follows RCW 19.122 with 811 notice 48 hours ahead and Engineer notice 48 hours before starting, plus access, storage and restoration duties (¶1.06–1.07, p.125; Verified).

| Summary | Project meetings coordinate the work, resolve conflicts, review progress and quality, and keep the work on schedule; attendees must have authority to act (¶1.01, p.126; Verified). Related sections include "00 25 13 Pre-Bid Conference", which is not in the 02 index (Issues 2.5), and "01 11 00", the accepted alias of 01 11 10 (¶1.02, p.126). nodes.label: Wiki note 00 24 13
nodes.note_text:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | 00 24 13 |
| Type | Spec section — Bidding Requirements (Part 1): bid item scope and measurement |
| Discipline | General |
| Revision/Date | Project manual Dec. 30, 2022 (main spec cover p.1, per 00 register); no section-level date |
| Summary | Describes where costs belong for each bid item in 00 41 00; each item is furnished, installed and tested, complete and in full operation before Owner acceptance (p.16; Verified). Item 1 WWTP Upgrade (LS) is paid per the approved Schedule of Values and covers all work in the Contract Documents; Items 2–5 cover trench safety (per WSDOT and OSHA — Unresolved: external reference, not staged), 12 bollards at Owner-chosen locations, SWPPP preparation with transfer of the NPDES construction stormwater permit, and SWPPP maintenance (¶1–5, pp.16–17; Verified except as tagged). Item 6 Electrical covers all E sheets and Division 26 (breakdowns in 26 05 00 and 26 80 00), and Item 7 Minor Changes covers changes of $100,000 or less that do not change Contract Time (¶6–7, p.17; Verified). Items 8–16 are unit-price contingencies for HMA, structural concrete, over-excavation and aggregates, and Item 17 is force-account SCADA/PLC programming; aggregate specs and force account defer to WSDOT 9-03 and 1-09.6 (¶8–17, pp.17–20; Unresolved: external reference, not staged). Bid Alternates 1 and 2 (Items 18, 19) add Type 316 stainless steel for Train 3 in-basin steel components above water (to 1 ft below) or throughout, excluding FRP weirs and covers, per 46 53 00 (¶18–19, p.20; Verified); the Item 18 conflict with Add. 4 is flagged in 02/03/04 (cited, not re-raised).

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | 00 41 00 |
| Type | Spec section — Bidding Requirements (Part 1): bid form, manufacturers list, equipment alternates |
| Discipline | General |
| Revision/Date | Project manual Dec. 30, 2022 (main spec cover p.1, per 00 register). Add. 4 (Feb 9, 2023) p.1 Clarification 5 cites "Bid Item #18" — conflict already flagged (02 item 1, 03 Merge flag, 04) |
| Summary | The form carries Base Bid Item 1 WWTP Upgrade (LS), unit-quantity Items 2–7, extra-work Items 8–17, Bid Alternate 1 (Item 18) and Bid Alternate 2 (Item 19), then 8.3% sales tax (Eastsound Sewer and Water District, San Juan County) and total bid (pp.23–25; Verified). The Owner pre-enters $100,000.00 for Item 7 Minor Changes (EST) and $100,000.00 for Item 17 Extra SCADA/PLC Programmer Services (FA) (pp.23–24; Verified). Base Bid Item 1 is based on the named manufacturers — Flygt submersible pumps, Smith and Loveless biological treatment, Fournier or Prime Solutions rotary fan press, Trojan UV, and Cummins/Kohler/Caterpillar/Generac generators — with Equipment Alternates A–E as lump-sum deductions; there is no pre-bid approval review and the bidder carries all redesign cost (pp.26–27; Verified). Mobilization is paid per WSDOT 1-09.7 (Unresolved: external reference, not staged); completion time points to "Supplementary Condition 15 – Completion Date", liquidated damages are per the General Conditions per calendar day, and the Owner may accept or reject bid prices within 60 days (p.27; Verified — the 60 days vs 45 days in 00 21 13 is Issues 1.4). Add. 4 p.1 Clarification 5 uses "Bid Item #18" for the temporary back-up generator while this form lists Item 18 as Train 3 stainless steel above water (p.25): Add. 4 governs the temporary generator requirements; the item number stays Unresolved per the existing flag (cited, not re-raised).

Submittals: disposal sites, gradation tests and proctors for imported material, geotextile cut sheets, and a traffic control plan per WSDOT 1-10 (¶1.05 C, ¶1.06; p.394 — Verified). APWA color-coded 2-in detectable warning tape is required over every new utility (red electric, blue water, green sewer, orange telephone/CATV, light blue air) and replaced where existing utilities are crossed (¶2.03; pp.394–395 — Verified). Open trench is limited to 200 ft ahead of pipe laying and trenches are closed or plated daily; owner notice is needed for traffic or parking disruptions (48 hours for shutdowns) (¶1.05 B, D, ¶3.02 F; pp.393–396 — Verified). | Equipment: Utility warning tape; trench safety systems; Spec sections: 00 33 00 and 01300 (cited; not in manual); 31 20 00; 31 32 11; 33 31 00; 33 41 00; 01 41 00; 01 45 00; Sheets: C7.4 (Detail 2); Addenda: — | C7.4; 31 20 00; 31 40 00; 04 Item 2 (Trench Safety) and Items 14, 16

nodes.note_text: Appendix F | Appendix — reference document (Part 4); states it is not part of the Contract Documents | Civil | Wilson Engineering, December 1, 2022 (p.612) (Verified); same subject as C0.7 (02 decision D) | Wilson Engineering's plan of interim operation lists the operational milestones from construction through start-up and states it is not part of the construction Contract Documents (§1.0–1.2; main spec p.614 — Verified). Scope summary: a third bullseye-style Bardenpho treatment train with new clarifier, an aerobic digester, UV disinfection, new dewatering equipment, a new influent flow splitter, new influent and 2W pump stations, a new blower building and stormwater improvements (§2.0; p.615 — Verified). Preliminary schedule: bid opening Feb 8, 2023, notice to proceed Mar 15, 2023, substantial completion July 2024 and final completion October 2024, with a CPM schedule due within 10 days of award and updated monthly per 01 31 00 (§3.0, Table 3-1; p.616 — Verified). Treatment stays continuous: the Contractor provides temporary piping from the existing chlorine disinfection chamber outlet to the 8-in effluent pipe just upstream of SSMH #1288, limits each disruption to 1 hour (influent pump station start-up with the flow splitter, the new 10-in effluent tie-in, the new transformer), lowers Train #2 with temporary pumps for the splitter tie-in, and submits a bypass plan; the detailed sequence is on C0.7 (§5.1–5.2; pp.618–619 — Verified). The Owner must have full use of the new generator before the old generator and switchgear are demolished, and at start-up new concrete basins get clean-water leakage tests and equipment gets operational tests per 01 45 00 and the equipment sections (§5.3.1, §6.0; p.619 — Verified).

nodes.label: Wiki note G0.3
nodes.note_text: G0.3 | Drawing sheet — general notes | General | BID SET; title block NOV 2, 2022; seal 11-02-2022 (Verified); revision block not read (Text sheet) | The Contractor must not interrupt District operations, must verify locations and depths of existing utilities (shown for information only), must report dimension discrepancies to the Engineer, and must repair damage to existing improvements within 48 hours (General Notes 1, 3–6; plans_1 p.3, G0.3 — Verified). Trenches and excavations must meet federal OSHA requirements, and trench shoring design and installation are the Contractor's full responsibility (General Note 7; plans_1 p.3, G0.3 — Verified). A 1-week notice to the District is required before any utility service disruption, and the Contractor must provide temporary equipment (power generator, pumps, piping) and an approved plan for all WWTP disruptions; the note cites 'Section 01 11 00', whose body number is 01 11 10 (General Note 10; plans_1 p.3, G0.3 — Verified; alias already flagged, 02 conflict 1). The Operation Plan makes the Contractor responsible for sequencing so the existing WWTP is not interrupted and for all temporary bypass pumping, piping, holding tanks and storage (Operation Plan 1–3; plans_1 p.3, G0.3 — Verified). Survey monuments disturbed by construction need WA DNR permits under WAC 332-120 and replacement by a registered land surveyor at Contractor cost; earthwork, concrete and asphalt repair are to be prioritized in dry-weather months; County inspections (footings, concrete structures, electrical, final) and S1.1 special inspections need 24-hour notice to Owner and Engineer (Schedule, Survey Monumentation and Construction Inspections notes; plans_1 p.3, G0.3 — Verified).

Units are Keystone Compaq II or approved equal to ASTM C1372: gray straight split face, running bond, 3,000 psi minimum, 8% maximum absorption, 8 x 18 x 12-in minimum, with two fiberglass pins per unit (¶2.02–2.03; pp.410–411 — Verified). The leveling pad (6 in minimum) and unit fill are crushed surfacing top course per WSDOT 9-03.9(3), and the pad is compacted to 95% standard or 92% modified Proctor (¶2.04–2.05, ¶3.02; p.411 — Verified; material Unresolved: external reference, not staged). The Owner's or Contractor's QA/QC representative inspects the excavation and tests foundation soils before the leveling pad; units are stacked no more than two courses ahead of fill, a footing drain and wall backfill are placed, and caps are glued (¶3.01, ¶3.03–3.04; pp.411–412 — Verified). As-built tolerances: ±1.5 in per 10 ft vertical and horizontal, batter within 2°, corners ±1 ft, gaps 1/2 in maximum (¶3.05; p.412 — Verified). | Equipment: Gravity block retaining wall; footing drain; Spec sections: 01 41 00; Sheets: C2.5; C7.8 Detail 1 (unavailable); Addenda: — | C2.5; C0.5 (Keyed Note 18); C7.8 (unavailable); 31 23 33 (¶2.04–2.06 wall drains); 33 31 00 (¶2.01 A footing drain pipe)

nodes.label: Wiki note Appendix C
nodes.note_text: Appendix C | Appendix — reference document (Part 4) | Civil | GeoEngineers File No. 0407-002-00: revised report Nov 8, 2022 (p.537) and report addendum Dec 16, 2022 (p.577) (Verified); date conflict with 31 20 00 already flagged (02 Merge flag 2) | GeoEngineers' revised report for 143 Cessna Road describes the site as fill (2–4.5 ft) over medium stiff to very stiff undifferentiated glacial drift (clay) to 19–24.5 ft, over glacial till, from borings B-1 to B-3 drilled Aug 10, 2020 (§§1.0, 2.3–2.4.1; main spec pp.542–543 — Verified). Groundwater in the B-3 monitoring well was 13.75 ft below grade (about El. 9.45 ft NAVD88) on Aug 24, 2020, with perched water likely in wet seasons; the report uses NAVD88 while the drawings use NGVD 1929 (§2.4.2; p.543 — Verified; see Issues). Design basis: Site Class D, not liquefiable, 2,500 psf allowable bearing on native drift or structural fill, settlement under 3/4 in, 6-in capillary break under slabs, and moisture-sensitive soils best worked in dry months (§3.0 summary; p.544 — Verified). Walls use 35 pcf active, 55 pcf at-rest and 300 pcf passive (drained), with an 18-in free-draining gravel zone and backfill compacted to 90–92%; structures get a perimeter drain of rigid perforated pipe (4 in minimum) in 6 in of 1-in washed gravel wrapped in non-woven geotextile (Mirafi 140N or similar), tight-lined to storm, and trench backfill compaction is 85% in landscaping, 90% below 2 ft and 95% in the top 2 ft under pavement (§§3.5, 3.6.2, 3.7; pp.548, 550 — Verified; conflicts, see Issues). The Dec 16, 2022 addendum suggests parking-area pavement of 2.5–3 in HMA over 3–4 in CSBC over 8–12 in gravel base, but its continuation page (p.578) and pages 539 and 576 have no text or image (p.577 — Verified; pages already deferred, 02 decision G).

| Type | Spec section — Division 01 General Requirements (Part 3) |
| Discipline | General |
| Revision/Date | Project manual Dec. 30, 2022 (main spec cover p.1, per 00 register); no section-level date |
| Summary | All material and equipment must be new, from established manufacturers, complete with accessories and guards, and installed per the manufacturer's printed instructions, with one instruction set kept on site and any conflict reported to the Owner (¶1.01.C, ¶1.03, p.146; Verified). Products arrive in labeled original containers, are inspected on delivery, are accepted only when unloading forces are on site, and are stored per the manufacturer with the Contractor fully responsible (¶1.04–1.05, pp.146–147; Verified). Named products set a quality standard; substitutes need the Owner's written acceptance before ordering, and requests are considered for 30 days after the Contract Date (¶1.06.A.4, ¶1.06.B.1, p.147; Verified; conflicts with the 10-day deadline in 01 33 00 — Issues 1.17). Each request goes in separately, six copies, with comparison data, schedule and cost effects; the Contractor pays the Engineer's review and redesign costs, and the Owner answers within two weeks (¶1.06.B.2–C, pp.147–148; Verified). Products likely to need later replacement must be standard, domestically produced items (¶1.06.A.2, p.147; Verified). |
| Tags | Equipment: none (applies to all products) · Spec: "01 30 00 Submittals" (not in library — Issues 2.5), 01 45 00, 01 33 00 · Sheets: none · Addenda: none |

nodes.label: Wiki note 43 11 00
nodes.note_text:
Document ID: 43 11 00 | Type: Specification section, 10 pages | Discipline: Process-Mechanical | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); pages numbered 431100-1 to -10 — already logged in 02 (#9)
Summary: Four identical Kaeser Com-paK DB 166 C positive-displacement blower packages (20 HP, 460 V 3-phase, VFD variable speed) serve the Biological Treatment System from the Blower Building, and one Kaeser Com-paK BB 52 C (5 HP, VFD) serves the aerobic digester from the existing metal building just north of the proposed blower building, "just west of" and "adjacent to" Train #2; Kaeser, Aerzen or approved equal (¶1.01 A–B p.462; ¶2.01 A pp.462–463; ¶O p.469). Design points: 315 scfm at 8.9 psig differential per biological blower (325 icfm, 10.1 psig max, relief at 12.0 psig, 17.4 bhp, 3,999 rpm, 207°F discharge) and 120 scfm at 4.0 psig for the digester blower (124 icfm, 6.6 psig max, relief at 8.0 psig, 3.8 bhp), each in a 72 dB(A) sound enclosure (¶2.01 A; ¶P p.470). Packages are oil-free tri-lobe and belt-driven with automatic belt tensioning, integral inlet filter-silencer and discharge silencer, spring relief valve, flexible connector, pressure, temperature and filter differential gauges, TEFC IP-55 motors with PTC thermistors at 18–60 Hz, 100,000-hour L10 bearings and vibration to VDI 3836 (¶2.01 B–K pp.463–467). Each blower is slip tested and run 30 minutes at maximum speed and differential, each package runs 15 minutes before shipment with a conformance certificate, the blower warranty is 60 months from shipment (other components 1 year from substantial completion), and submittals per 01 33 00 are catalog data, fabrication and installation drawings, and O&M information (¶2.01 L–N pp.467–468; ¶1.02 A p.462). Controls sit in a NEMA 12 cabinet with the VFDs in the MCC, and the contractor wires the over-temperature, over-pressure and motor temperature sensors to the PLC control panel and supplies tees, supports and fittings (¶2.01 Q, ¶3.01 A p.471).

| E8.1 | Drawing — control panel exterior, interior door and backpanel elevations | Controls | BID SET; title block 09-12-2022; revision block blank; set p.85 of 96 (Verified; revision block Verified-Visual) | Exterior: NEMA 4X Type 316 stainless steel enclosure with drip shield, sized to hold all equipment, on a concrete equipment pad "per civil specifications"; key note 1 calls for local control of the influent pumps, seal-fail and overtemperature wiring and instrumentation, with controls on an internal swing-out door behind a lockable outer door (plans_11 p.5) [Verified; enclosure label Verified-Visual]. Swing-out door: influent wet well level display; for each of pumps 1–4 a hand-off-auto switch and run, fail, seal-fail and overtemperature lights with reset; four float-activated lights with float test buttons (plans_11 p.5) [Verified-Visual; labels also in text]. Backpanel: main 480 V disconnect; panel LP2 with its transformer and overcurrent protection; area light hand-off-auto and GFCI receptacle; panel heater and thermostat; power distribution block and phase monitor; pump circuit breakers and full-voltage NEMA starters for influent pumps 1–4; field terminals for motor connections; network switch and PLC rack; DC power supply and UPS; interposing relays; seal-fail relays; intrinsically safe area with barriers for the floats and level transducer (plans_11 p.5) [Verified]. Key notes 2–4: flow meter transmitters for influent, Cell 1 (future space), Cell 2, Cell 3 and plant drain, with coil and electrode cables from the meter vaults; seal-fail and overtemperature relays (Mini-CAS or equal) furnished by the pump manufacturer and coordinated by the system integrator; field conduits not shown — route all raceway shown on the plans to the influent control panel (plans_11 p.5) [Verified].

| E8.2 | Drawing — control panel power and pump control wiring diagrams | Controls | BID SET; title block 09-12-2022; revision block blank; set p.86 of 96 (Verified; revision block Verified-Visual). Title differs from cover index — 01 log item 6 | Schematic power wiring: 480 V 3-phase into a power distribution block with a surge suppressor, a phase-fail relay and control transformer CPT1 (120 VAC control power), then a breaker, motor starter and overload for each of pumps 1–4 (plans_11 p.6) [Verified-Visual; labels also in text]. Pump data as printed: pump no.1 and no.2 "XP" 3 HP, 4.8 FLA; pump no.3 and no.4 "XP" 5 HP, 7.6 FLA — matching the E6.1 horsepower for IP-1 to IP-4 (plans_11 p.6; plans_10 p.2) [Verified-Visual]. Pump control wiring, typical for each of 4 pumps: hand-off-auto; in auto the starter runs on a PLC contact or, in parallel, the high-float contact; the starter coil is interlocked by the overtemperature relay, the phase-fail relay and the overload; lights for pump running, overtemperature, seal fail and overload (plans_11 p.6) [Verified-Visual]. Seal-fail/overtemperature relay per pump, wired to the pump housing sensors (T1, T2) with a reset, driving relays CROT and CRSF (plans_11 p.6) [Verified-Visual; relay labels also in text]. General note 1: the system integrator provides the detailed panel design; only major components are specified (plans_11 p.6) [Verified].

| E8.3 | Drawing — PLC digital input wiring and high-level float control circuit | Controls | BID SET; title block 09-12-2022; revision block blank; set p.87 of 96 (Verified; revision block Verified-Visual) | Two Allen-Bradley 1769-IQ16 16-point input cards, all 32 channels used: influent pumps 1–4 (hand, auto, running, fault, seal fail, overtemperature — six each), wet well floats F1–F4 through relays ISR-F1B to ISR-F4B, ventilation fans 1–3 "called to run" from the ventilation control panel, and phase fail (plans_11 p.7) [Verified-Visual]. General note 2 calls for added I/O cards to give at least 20% spare inputs, not shown; with 32 of 32 inputs used that means at least 7 more inputs, a third card (plans_11 p.7) [Verified-Visual; card count Inferred by arithmetic]. Each pump input block is labeled "INFLUENT PUMP n: MCC", and pump 2 shows "VFD FAULT" with no "auto selected" input, unlike pumps 1, 3 and 4 — see Issues (plans_11 p.7) [Verified-Visual]. High-level float control circuit (hardwired backup): each wet well high-level float passes an intrinsic safety barrier (relays ISR-FnA/FnB), lights a "high float activated" panel light, has a test button, and "starts pump n" through relay CRHn with a time-off-delay relay TDRn, 0–60 s; key note 1 sets true-off delay, field-adjusted to wet well pump-down rate (plans_11 p.7) [Verified-Visual; key note Verified]. Float n is wired to pump n (F1 to 3 HP pump 1), while the E4.2 level table assigns F1 and F2 to the large pumps — see Issues (plans_11 p.7; plans_9 p.7) [Verified-Visual; large-pump reading Inferred from horsepower].

| E6.2 | Drawing — panel schedules (Visual sheet) | Electrical | BID SET; title block 09-12-2022; schedules dated September 15, 2022; set p.75 of 96 (Verified; schedule dates Verified-Visual) | Three panel schedules (MDP, LP1, LP2); the text layer carries only the titles, so every schedule entry is read from the page image (plans_10 p.3) [Verified-Visual]. Panel MDP: 480Y/277V 3-ph 4-W, 400 A bus, 400 A main lugs only, surface mounted, 42,000 AIC; circuits 1-3-5 Blower Building MCC (400 A 3-pole, 60,000 VA per phase) and 2-4-6 transformer for existing building 480–208Y/120V (125 A 3-pole, 15,000 VA per phase); circuits 7–30 spaces; connected and demand 225.0 kVA, 270.6 A (plans_10 p.3) [Verified-Visual]. Panel LP2 (Influent Pump Station panel): 120/240 V 1-ph 3-W, 100 A bus, 60 A main breaker, 10,000 AIC; pump station control circuits, wall pack lighting, ventilation control panel, EF-3, EF-4, EF-5 (Treatment Building, 1,127 VA each), H2S and methane sensors, polymer feed pump and influent sampler receptacles, six spares; demand 7.8 kVA, 32.3 A; circuit numbers match the E4.1 callouts (plans_10 p.3) [Verified-Visual]. | E6.1 | Drawing — one-line diagram, key notes, load calculation table | Electrical | BID SET; title block 09-12-2022; set p.74 of 96 (Verified) | Service and distribution: OPALCO 225 kVA 480Y/277V pad-mount transformer → P-SEC → CT enclosure and utility meter → P-ATS → ATS (400 A service entrance, 4-wire 3-pole, NEMA 12, delayed open transition) with the 125 kW / 156 kVA standby diesel generator (sound-attenuated outdoor enclosure, sub-base fuel tank, 250/3, P-GEN) → P-MDP → MDP (480Y/277V, main lugs only, SPD) → 400/3 to the MCC and 125/3 to transformer TS (75 kVA 480–208Y/120V), which re-feeds the existing Office Building 400 A I-Line panel and, through its 200/3, Panel TPS (plans_10 p.2) [Verified-Visual; tags also in text]. MCC (480 V 3-ph 4-W, Blower Building): 400/3 main, power monitor with (3) 400:5 CTs, SPD; 30/3 units for TCP-1 and TCP-2 (greyed, "future") and TCP-3; 60/3 for dewatering skid DW-1 and for the IPS panel; 60/2 to T2 (20 kVA 480–120/240V) and its load center; ten VFDs with line reactors — 2W-P1 and 2W-P2 (20/3, 5 HP), WP-1, WP-2 (swing) and SD-1 (15/3, 3 HP), all five with dV/dt reactors, BL-1 to BL-4 (35/3, 20 HP) and DB (20/3, 5 HP) (plans_10 p.2) [Verified-Visual]. IPS Influent Pump Station control panel (480 V 3-ph 3-W, NEMA 4X SS): 60/3 main, contactor-and-overload starters for IP-1 and IP-2 (15/3, 3 HP) and IP-3 and IP-4 (20/3, 5 HP), and 30/2 to T3 (10 kVA 480–120/240V) and its load center; a local disconnect is drawn at each motor (plans_10 p.2) [Verified-Visual]. Key notes: 1 the manufacturer sets VFD overcurrent protection ratings; 2 3% line-side reactors on all VFDs; 3 dV/dt load-side reactors on VFD motor runs over 50 ft; 4 outdoor control panel and disconnect enclosures Type 316 SS; 5 aeration blower disconnects are on the MCC within sight of the motors (plans_10 p.2) [Verified; numbering Verified-Visual].

| 26 05 00 | Specification section | Electrical | Project manual cover dated Dec. 30, 2022 (p.1); Division 26 TOC dated 09/12/2022 (p.268) — per 00 register; section pages 1–13 of 13 = main spec pp.269–281 (Verified) | Drawings and specifications are complementary; motor horsepower on the drawings is an estimate for equipment furnished under other sections, with overloads sized to actual nameplate current (¶1.011 B–C, p.274) [Verified]. Submittals (¶1.012, p.274): electronic PDF with an index, identified by section and paragraph or equipment, each sheet naming the equipment and part number with manufacturer, model, nameplate data, dimensions and local representative; largely incomplete packages are returned unreviewed; variances requested in writing [Verified]. Construction power and downtime (¶1.015–1.016, p.276): the contractor provides and pays for a dedicated construction power service and its energy; power to the operating plant is kept at all times, with one week notice to the District before any utility disruption, and temporary equipment (generator, pumps, piping) plus an Owner/Engineer-approved written plan for any disruption over 20 minutes [Verified]. Utility interface (¶3.03, pp.279–280): OPALCO serves the site and the Owner pays utility charges; the contractor provides the new 480Y/277V underground secondary from the existing transformer pad to the CT enclosure, service-rated ATS and 400 A panel, the CT enclosure and meter bases, demolition of the existing 208V service (raceway, conductors, CT enclosure, meter base, generator, ATS) and temporary power to hold downtime to 20 minutes; the Utility removes the existing 208V transformer, sets the new 480V transformer on the existing pad and provides the CTs and meter [Verified].

| 26 22 13 | Specification section | Electrical | Project manual cover dated Dec. 30, 2022 (p.1); Division 26 TOC dated 09/12/2022 (p.268) — per 00 register; section pages 1–3 of 3 = main spec pp.297–299 (Verified) | Dry-type transformers 600 V and below for distribution, lighting and control; NRTL-listed; sizes and windings per the drawings; ANSI/IEEE C57.12.01 and UL 506; GE, Square D, Westinghouse or equal; equipment must fit the space shown (¶1.01–1.04, ¶2.01, p.297) [Verified]. Construction: 15 kVA and above with two 2.5% taps above and four below rated primary voltage; copper terminals in the bottom third; 15 kVA and smaller weatherproof non-ventilated and wall-mountable, larger indoor units drip-proof ventilated and 20 kVA and larger floor-mounted (¶2.05–2.08, p.298) [Verified]. Document ID: C3.3 | Type: Drawing — equipment plan | Discipline: Civil (per 01); process-mechanical content | Revision/Date: image-only page; BID SET, title block NOV 2, 2022, page 28 of 96 read from the image; seal 11-02-2022 (the only text in the layer); revision block blank
Summary: Plan of the new Train 3 bullseye tank: 32.00' inner and 34.00' outer wall diameter, 12" walls and a 12" footing extension, around an 18'-0" clarifier (R300, 500.7 SF) with a 5'-0" feed well, sludge scraper arms and scraper arm drive, skimmer arm, scum skimmer airlift, a 3'-0" clarifier bridge and a 2' peripheral clarifier walkway with handrail. The annulus holds Aeration Zone #1 (3,983 CF), Aeration Zone #2 (1,322 CF), Anoxic Zone #1 (2,097 CF) and Anoxic Zone #2 (1,175 CF), with plenum diffusers, an adjustable weir, DO #1 and DO #2 DO/pH sensors (detail 1/C7.4), two submersible mixers, a RAS airlift weir box, a nitrate recycle weir box and a 6" nitrate recycle (MLR) pipe; a 3" RAS airlift sludge duct and a 10" clarifier inlet pipe run inside the clarifier. Connections: Train 3 8" influent IE 20.08, Train 3 8" effluent IE 20.00, 2" WAS/clarifier drain to the WAS pump, and a 6" air inlet. Two davit crane assemblies and a prefab aluminum ladder assembly connected to the access platform (clarifier bridge) are shown; note 1 requires partitions reinforced for individual zone dewatering (not shown for clarity).
Tags: Equipment — Train 3 tank, clarifier mechanism, clarifier bridge and walkway, ladder, davit cranes (2), submersible mixers (2), plenum diffusers, DO #1, DO #2, RAS airlift, nitrate recycle airlift, weir boxes, zone partitions · Spec sections — none printed · Sheets — detail 1/C7.4 · Addenda — none
Related documents: C3.4, C3.5; G0.5, G0.7; 46 53 00; 46 41 23 and 10 73 05 [by title, Inferred]; S2.1 "Train 3 Plans & Section" (per 01 title); C7.4 (Civil & Site stack). Issues 2, 3; Open check 3, closed: 46 41 23.

Document ID: 10 73 05 | Type: Specification section, 3 pages | Discipline: Process-Mechanical (lane per 02, decision D) | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); no section-level date
Summary: The contractor furnishes and installs a molded, UV-protected, opaque FRP cover over the Train 3 clarifier weir launder and weir, in curved sections at least 4 ft long, each a single section on two pivoting brackets opening toward the tank center, with spring-loaded latches, an optional stainless tether, fixed or vertical panels at the bridge support, no piano hinges, no inspection hatches, and not walk-on except for a reinforced walk-on section at the launder entry (¶1.01 A–H pp.243–244). Panels are isophthalic polyester with UV suppression, at least 35% glass by weight (ASTM D2584-18), nominal 1/4" thick and no more than 55 lb each, with tensile 26,000 psi, flexural 30,000 psi, flexural modulus 1.9×10^6 psi, Barcol 50, notched Izod 20 ft-lb/in and water absorption 0.25% max; fasteners, handles, hinges and latches are stainless (¶3.01 B–G pp.244–245). Submittals per 01 33 00 are catalog data and O&M information (¶2.01 A p.244); the contractor adds a 1-year parts-and-labor extended warranty from substantial completion (¶1.02 A p.244); three sets of wear parts are furnished (¶3.02 p.245); and the manufacturer provides installation certification, 2 days of start-up and field testing and 1 day of operator training (¶4.02 p.245). ¶3.01 A, under the launder cover heading, repeats the packaged sludge pump paragraph of 22 13 36 ¶2.01 A word for word (Edson peristaltic pumps, 3 HP, a VFD per pump) — Issue 20. The section runs in four parts (Part 2 submittals, Part 3 products, Part 4 execution).

nodes.label: Wiki note 46 41 23
nodes.note_text:
Document ID: 46 41 23 | Type: Specification section, 5 pages | Discipline: Process-Mechanical | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); no section-level date
Summary: Furnish and install two mixer assemblies, two masts and two davit cranes, with one mixer in each anoxic zone of new Train #3 (¶1.01 A p.486). Mixers are at most 5 HP nameplate, 460 V 3-phase, with 316 Ti stainless propeller (EverClean blades), shaft, housing and frame, a duplex stainless casing cover, silicon carbide double mechanical seals in an oil chamber, a plug-and-receptacle power cable with resin-sealed entry, three PTC thermal switches and a moisture detector, bearings over 100,000 hours B10, maintenance intervals of at least 16,000 hours or 2 years, and 10 starts per hour (¶2.01 A–B, F pp.486–489). Each mixer rides a permanent 4"-square stainless guide mast with sockets at 10 ft max, a 14-position rotary top plate and an adjustable stop bracket (or a floor mounting pedestal), and two portable stainless lifting davits with manual brake winches mount on the top mast bracket, with removable handrail or chain sections so mixers need not be lifted over the handrail (¶2.01 C–E p.488); the mixer supplier furnishes motor-sensor monitoring relays that others install in the motor control panel (¶2.01 B.4 p.487). Controls follow 26 80 00 ¶3.09 B (¶2.02 p.489); submittals per 01 33 00 are catalog data with wiring diagrams and O&M information (¶1.02 A p.486); the contractor gives a 1-year parts-and-labor extended warranty (¶1.03 A); three sets of wear parts are furnished (¶2.03); and testing covers factory checks (balance, leakage, electrical, insulation, no-load rotation), field testing after installation, 2 days of start-up and 1 day of training (¶2.04 p.489; ¶3.01 B–3.02 p.490). The same two mixers are also specified in 46 53 00, whose single-source and precedence clauses overlap this section (Issue 30).

nodes.label: Wiki note 46 53 00
nodes.note_text:
Document ID: 46 53 00 | Type: Specification section, 10 pages | Discipline: Process-Mechanical | Revision/Date: main spec issue Dec. 30, 2022 (per 00); no section-level date
Summary: Specifies Train 3 ("3rd Train") as a single bullseye multistage anoxic/aerobic activated sludge system, basis of design Smith & Loveless Model R Oxigest, with the in-basin aeration system, mixers, clarifier equipment, instrumentation and controls supplied and guaranteed by one manufacturer (¶1.01 A p.492; ¶1.03 A p.493); this section's valves, equipment, materials and controls supersede other specifications (¶1.03 F p.493), and alternate systems are bid as an Equipment Alternate with a submittal package (¶1.03 E, ¶1.04 p.493). Design influent is 63,333 gpd average to 178 gpm peak hour, with effluent BOD5 and TSS 30 mg/L and TIN 8 mg/L (¶1.02 p.492); the supplier gives a 2-year process performance guarantee with the equipment submittal and a 12-month mechanical guarantee from Substantial Completion (¶1.05 A, C p.494). The tank has a reinforced concrete outer wall and structural steel plate inner walls of at least 1/4" (¶2.01 B.1 p.494), 32 ft ID, 15.5 ft static depth and 16.9 ft overall wall height, 43,000 gal of annular aeration and 26,508 gal of anoxic volume in two compartments, each with a 5 HP 460 V submersible mixer, and 240 scfm through S&L medium bubble diffusers plus 75 scfm of airlift air, 315 scfm total (¶2.01 C.1 p.495; header and drop pipes ¶2.01 C.2 p.496).

nodes.label: Wiki note S2.1
nodes.note_text:
- **Document ID:** S2.1
- **Type:** Drawing — structural plan, section and reinforcing details for the Train 3 tank
- **Discipline:** Structural (Kingworks)
- **Revision/Date:** Title block 10-15-2021; revision 2 "Bid Set" TH 9/6/22 [plans_8 p.1 — Verified-Visual]. No Add. 4 entry.
- **Summary:** Train 3 is a circular cast-in-place tank: a 12" concrete wall on a 12" mat slab foundation with a raised center pedestal [plans_8 p.1, S2.1 Detail 1 — Verified-Visual]. Wall reinforcing is #5 horizontal at 12" o.c. each face (Grade 75 bars, laps staggered per Detail 5) and #5 vertical at 12" o.c. each face with 3" clear, plus (2) #4 horizontal at the top [plans_8 p.1, Detail 4 — Verified-Visual]. Slab reinforcing is continuous #5 at 12" o.c. with #5 radial bars at 12" o.c. at the outer edge (top shown, bottom similar; 2" clear top, 3" clear bottom), the pedestal has #5 radial bars at 16" o.c., and the slab center adds #5 × 8'-0" top and bottom bars with radial bars ending at 3'-0" and 1'-0" diameter rings [plans_8 p.1, Details 1–3 — Verified-Visual]. Detail 4 requires a hydrophilic waterstop (submit for approval), a grout surface per spec, and subgrade preparation per the structural notes and geotech report, and shows "guardrail, mechanical equipment, and ladders per civil" [plans_8 p.1, Detail 4 — Verified-Visual]. Horizontal laps may align vertically only at every third bar or more, with lap length per 3/S4.1 [plans_8 p.1, Detail 5 — Verified-Visual]; the S4.1 table covers Grade 60 uncoated bars only while these horizontal bars are Grade 75 [plans_8 p.5; Add. 4 p.10, S4.1 Detail 3 Note 1 — Verified-Visual; Unresolved: need Grade 75 lap lengths — Issues, Conflicts #2].

| Summary | Bidders must be registered with WA Labor & Industries, corporations with the WA Secretary of State, and be regularly employed in this type of work (¶1, p.11; Verified). Interpretations and changes bind only by Addendum, substitutions are not considered before bid receipt, and bidders must acknowledge addenda in the bid (¶3.C–D, ¶4.B, p.11; Verified). Subcontractors individually over 10% of the Contract Sum are listed with the bid or within one hour of bid time, and bid security is 5% of the total bid (¶5.C, ¶7.A, p.12; Verified). Award goes to the lowest responsible responsive bidder within 45 days of opening, in any combination of bid schedules and alternates; the contract bond is the full contract amount and stays in effect until one year after Substantial Completion (¶12–14, pp.13–14; Verified). The awardee returns the signed contract within 10 working days of award (¶15.A) but ¶16.A says 10 calendar days (p.14; Issues 1.3, Unresolved); no work on site before Notice to Proceed (¶15.C, p.14; Verified). |

nodes.label: Wiki note 00 53 00
nodes.note_text:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | 00 53 00 |
| Type | Spec section — Contracting Requirements (Part 2): funding-agency contract clauses and bid forms |
| Discipline | General |
| Revision/Date | Ecology WPCRF Specifications Insert "Revised 1/22/21" (p.41); project manual Dec. 30, 2022 |
| Summary | Ecology WPCRF clauses are incorporated and take precedence in any conflict within the contract (p.41; Verified) — not placed in the 00 73 00 SC 2 order (Issues 2.7). Required with the bid: Certification of Nonsegregated Facilities (Attachment 3), EPA DBE forms 6100-4 and 6100-3 (one per DBE sub; forms on the Ecology website), and the complete Bidders List (p.41; Verified); pp.45–46 then allow the DBE forms and the Bidders List "as part of the bid, or within one hour" after bid time (Verified) — timing conflicts inside this section and with 00 43 93 and 01 33 00 (Issues 1.6). Site and records clauses: safe access for Ecology and EPA, separate auditable project records kept 3 years after final audit, no discharge to state waters without Ecology approval, a funding-recognition sign visible from nearby roadways for the life of the project with Department logos, and the Inadvertent Discovery Plan kept on site with work stopped on any discovery (pp.41–42; Verified). American Iron and Steel applies to treatment works: iron and steel products (pipe and fittings, castings, hydrants, tanks, flanges, restraints, valves, structural steel, reinforced precast, construction materials) must be US-produced unless waived, with certification on request and damages for non-compliance (pp.42–43; Verified). Davis-Bacon, debarment, DBE six good faith efforts, 30-day sub payment, EEO (EO 11246) and segregated-facilities clauses follow, with Attachment 1 (DB terms, pp.53–61), Attachment 2 (DB wage determination — an unfilled placeholder, p.62; Issues 2.4), Attachment 3 (p.64) and Attachment 4 notice to labor unions (p.65) (pp.43–65; Verified).

nodes.note_text:

| Document ID | 00 54 00 |
| Type | Spec section — Contracting Requirements (Part 2): federal/state grant contract clauses |
| Discipline | General |
| Revision/Date | Commerce CDBG Conditions [Attachment 7-A(1)] (p.66); HUD-4010 (07/2021) labor standards (p.68); project manual Dec. 30, 2022 |
| Summary | Sixteen Commerce CDBG clauses apply, from records access through ADA (TOC p.66; Verified). Records are kept 3 years after final audit; contracts over $100,000 need 100% performance and 100% payment bonds; the Owner secures lands and rights-of-way before construction; every subcontractor needs the Owner's prior written approval and SAM.gov verification (p.67; Verified). HUD-4010 federal labor standards require weekly certified payrolls, and state prevailing wage (RCW 39.12) requires L&I-approved Statements of Intent before any payment and Affidavits of Wages Paid before retainage release under RCW 60.28.010 (pp.68–74; Verified). This is a Section 3 covered project under 24 CFR Part 75, and EO 11246 sets a 6.9% female participation goal in each trade, with minority goals by DOL reference (pp.74–76; Verified). The EO 11246 "covered area" is an unfilled placeholder (p.77; Issues 2.3, Unresolved). |

| Summary | Under RCW 60.28 the contractor elects how retainage is held; with no election, the District holds it in its Current Expense Fund without interest until 30 days after final acceptance (p.87; Verified). Other options are an interest-bearing account or listed securities with interest to the contractor, or a bond-in-lieu for the entire 5% retainage, in which case the contractor must accept like bonds from subs and release their retainage within 30 days (p.87; Verified). Retainage is normally released 30–45 days after final acceptance or after Employment Security and Department of Revenue clearance, whichever is longer (p.87; Verified); SC 17 sets release within 30 days of final acceptance plus releases (00 73 00 p.91). |

Appendix G | Appendix — reference document (Part 4) | General | Ecology form ECY 070-560 (09/2016) (p.622) (Verified) | Ecology-format plan and procedures for unanticipated discovery of cultural resources and human skeletal remains, for this project in San Juan County, Section 11, T37N, R2W (§1; main spec p.622 — Verified). It lists what a discovery looks like (shell middens, bone, charcoal-stained soil, stone tools, historic cans and bottles) and requires stopping work, protecting the area and notifying the District project manager (Jason Bradshaw) and Ecology (Ken Ziebart; cultural resource alternate Liz Ellis), with Drayton Archaeology named if a monitoring plan is in place (§§2–3; pp.622–623 — Verified). A qualified archaeologist assesses finds and DAHP, tribes and agencies are notified; human remains are treated with dignity, not photographed, and handled under the special procedures in §5 (§§4–5; pp.624–625 — Verified). Finds are documented by a professional archaeologist, a technical report is due within 90 days of fieldwork, and work outside the discovery area may continue (§§6–7; pp.626–627 — Verified). Pages 628–637 have no text or image (already deferred, 02 decision G). | Equipment: —; Spec sections: —; Sheets: —; Addenda: — | 31 10 00; 31 20 00; 31 23 33 (ground-disturbing work)
